    S.end_date
FROM
    Users AS U,
    Subscriptions AS S
WHERE
    U.user_id = S.user_id
    AND S.end_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '30 day' AND S.is_active = TRUE;

SELECT U.username, S.start_date FROM Users AS U, Subscriptions AS S WHERE U.user_id = S.user_id;

SELECT S.sub_id, T.tier_name FROM Subscriptions AS S, Tiers AS T WHERE S.tier_id = T.tier_id;

SELECT U.email, S.is_active FROM Users AS U, Subscriptions AS S WHERE U.user_id = S.user_id;

SELECT T.tier_name, T.price_monthly FROM Tiers AS T, Subscriptions AS S WHERE T.tier_id = S.tier_id;

SELECT U.username, T.tier_name FROM Users AS U, Subscriptions AS S, Tiers AS T WHERE U.user_id = S.user_id AND S.tier_id = T.tier_id;

SELECT S.start_date, S.end_date FROM Subscriptions AS S, Users AS U WHERE S.user_id = U.user_id;

SELECT T.tier_name, COUNT(S.sub_id) FROM Tiers AS T, Subscriptions AS S WHERE T.tier_id = S.tier_id GROUP BY T.tier_name;

SELECT U.username, U.email FROM Users AS U, Subscriptions AS S WHERE U.user_id = S.user_id AND S.is_active = TRUE;

text_es: Schema: Assets (asset_id, filename, file_type, upload_date, uploaded_by), Tags (tag_id, tag_name), AssetTags (asset_id, tag_id). Queries: 1. Find all assets with a specific tag. 2. List all tags associated with a particular asset. 3. Insert a new asset and associate it with a tag. 4. Remove a specific tag from an asset. 5. Count the number of assets per file type.
text_nat:
SELECT A.filename
FROM Assets A
JOIN AssetTags AT ON A.asset_id = AT.asset_id
JOIN Tags T ON AT.tag_id = T.tag_id
WHERE T.tag_name = 'holiday';

SELECT T.tag_name
FROM Tags T
JOIN AssetTags AT ON T.tag_id = AT.tag_id
JOIN Assets A ON AT.asset_id = A.asset_id

text_es: Schema: Customers (customer_id, customer_name, email), Transactions (transaction_id, customer_id, amount, transaction_date), LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_balance, last_updated). Queries: 1. Get the current loyalty points for a customer. 2. Update a customer's loyalty points after a transaction (add points). 3. Find all customers with more than X points. 4. Get the total transaction amount for each customer. 5. List customers who haven't earned points in the last 90 days.
text_nat:
SELECT
    lp.points_balance
FROM
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp
JOIN
    Customers AS c
ON
    lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE
    c.customer_name = 'John Doe';

UPDATE LoyaltyPoints
SET
    points_balance = points_balance + 10
WHERE
    customer_id = (SELECT customer_id FROM Customers WHERE customer_name = 'Jane Smith');

SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    lp.points_balance
FROM
    Customers AS c
JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp
ON
    c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.points_balance > 100;

SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    SUM(t.amount) AS total_transaction_amount
FROM
    Customers AS c
JOIN
    Transactions AS t
ON
    c.customer_id = t.customer_id
GROUP BY
    c.customer_name;

SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    c.email
FROM
    Customers AS c
LEFT JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp
ON
    c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.last_updated < DATE('now', '-90 days') OR lp.last_updated IS NULL;

SELECT

FROM

JOIN
    Transactions AS t
ON

ON

ON

text_es: Schema: Courses (course_id, course_title, instructor_id), Lectures (lecture_id, course_id, lecture_title, lecture_date, duration_minutes), Students (student_id, student_name). Queries: 1. List all lectures for a specific course. 2. Find all courses taught by a particular instructor. 3. Insert a new lecture for an existing course. 4. Update the duration of a lecture. 5. Get the total duration of lectures for each course.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all lectures for a specific course
SELECT l.lecture_title, l.lecture_date, l.duration_minutes
FROM Lectures l
JOIN Courses c ON l.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE c.course_title = 'Database Fundamentals';

-- 2. Find all courses taught by a particular instructor
SELECT c.course_title
FROM Courses c
WHERE c.instructor_id = 101;

-- 3. Insert a new lecture for an existing course
INSERT INTO Lectures (course_id, lecture_title, lecture_date, duration_minutes)
SELECT c.course_id, 'New Lecture Topic', '2023-11-20', 90
FROM Courses c
WHERE c.course_title = 'Advanced SQL';

-- 4. Update the duration of a lecture
UPDATE Lectures
SET duration_minutes = 75
WHERE lecture_id = 5;

-- 5. Get the total duration of lectures for each course
SELECT c.course_title, SUM(l.duration_minutes) AS total_duration_minutes
FROM Courses c
JOIN Lectures l ON c.course_id = l.course_id
GROUP BY c.course_title;

text_es: Schema: Recipes (recipe_id, recipe_name, instructions), Ingredients (ingredient_id, ingredient_name, unit_of_measure), RecipeIngredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id, quantity_needed), Inventory (ingredient_id, quantity_on_hand, last_restocked). Queries: 1. List all ingredients for a specific recipe, with quantities. 2. Find recipes that can be made with current inventory (assuming enough of all ingredients). 3. Update the quantity on hand for an ingredient in inventory. 4. Get a list of ingredients that are low in stock (e.g., quantity_on_hand < 10). 5. Find recipes that use a particular ingredient.
text_nat:
SELECT
    i.ingredient_name,
    ri.quantity_needed,
    i.unit_of_measure
FROM
    Ingredients AS i
JOIN
    RecipeIngredients AS ri ON i.ingredient_id = ri.ingredient_id
WHERE
    ri.recipe_id = 1;

SELECT
    r.recipe_name
FROM
    Recipes AS r
JOIN
    RecipeIngredients AS ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
GROUP BY
    r.recipe_id, r.recipe_name
HAVING
    COUNT(CASE WHEN ri.quantity_needed <= (SELECT i.quantity_on_hand FROM Inventory AS i WHERE i.ingredient_id = ri.ingredient_id) THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) = COUNT(ri.ingredient_id);

UPDATE Inventory
SET
    quantity_on_hand = 50
WHERE
    ingredient_id = 3;

SELECT
    i.ingredient_name,
    inv.quantity_on_hand
FROM
    Ingredients AS i
JOIN
    Inventory AS inv ON i.ingredient_id = inv.ingredient_id
WHERE
    inv.quantity_on_hand < 10;

SELECT
    r.recipe_name
FROM
    Recipes AS r
JOIN
    RecipeIngredients AS ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
JOIN
    Ingredients AS i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id
WHERE
    i.ingredient_name = 'Flour';

    r.recipe_name,
    i.ingredient_name
FROM
    Recipes AS r
JOIN
    RecipeIngredients AS ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
JOIN
    Ingredients AS i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id
JOIN
    Inventory AS inv ON i.ingredient_id = inv.ingredient_id
WHERE
    inv.quantity_on_hand > 0;

SELECT
    i.ingredient_name,
    inv.last_restocked
FROM
    Ingredients AS i
JOIN
    Inventory AS inv ON i.ingredient_id = inv.ingredient_id
ORDER BY
    inv.last_restocked DESC;

Schema: Conferences (conference_id, conference_name, start_date), Speakers (speaker_id, speaker_name, bio, company), Sessions (session_id, conference_id, speaker_id, session_title, start_time, end_time). Queries: 1. List all sessions at a specific conference. 2. Find all sessions presented by a particular speaker. 3. Insert a new session for a conference with a speaker. 4. Update a speaker's bio. 5. Get the count of sessions per speaker.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all sessions at a specific conference.
SELECT
  s.session_title,
  s.start_time,
  s.end_time
FROM Sessions s
JOIN Conferences c ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id
WHERE
  c.conference_name = 'Tech Summit 2024';

-- 2. Find all sessions presented by a particular speaker.
SELECT
  s.session_title,
  c.conference_name,
  s.start_time
FROM Sessions s
JOIN Speakers sp ON s.speaker_id = sp.speaker_id
WHERE
  sp.speaker_name = 'Alice Wonderland';

-- Separate query 1
SELECT s.session_title FROM Sessions s JOIN Conferences c ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id;

-- Separate query 2
SELECT sp.speaker_name FROM Speakers sp JOIN Sessions s ON sp.speaker_id = s.speaker_id;

-- 3. Insert a new session for a conference with a speaker.
INSERT INTO Sessions (
  conference_id,
  speaker_id,
  session_title,
  start_time,
  end_time
)
SELECT
  c.conference_id,
  sp.speaker_id,
  'Advanced SQL Techniques',
  '2024-11-15 14:00:00',
  '2024-11-15 15:00:00'
FROM Conferences c
JOIN Speakers sp ON c.conference_name = 'DevOps World 2024'
AND sp.speaker_name = 'Bob The Builder';

-- Separate query 3
SELECT c.conference_name FROM Conferences c JOIN Sessions s ON c.conference_id = s.conference_id;

-- 4. Update a speaker's bio.
UPDATE Speakers
SET
  bio = 'Experienced software engineer focusing on cloud architecture.'
WHERE
  speaker_name = 'Alice Wonderland';

-- Separate query 4
SELECT s.session_title FROM Sessions s JOIN Speakers sp ON s.speaker_id = sp.speaker_id;

-- 5. Get the count of sessions per speaker.
SELECT
  sp.speaker_name,
  COUNT(s.session_id) AS session_count
FROM Speakers sp
JOIN Sessions s ON sp.speaker_id = s.speaker_id
GROUP BY
  sp.speaker_name;

-- Separate query 5
SELECT c.start_date FROM Conferences c JOIN Sessions s ON c.conference_id = s.conference_id;

-- Separate query 6
SELECT sp.company FROM Speakers sp JOIN Sessions s ON sp.speaker_id = s.speaker_id;

-- Separate query 7
SELECT s.session_title FROM Sessions s JOIN Conferences c ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id;

-- Separate query 8
SELECT c.conference_name FROM Conferences c JOIN Sessions s ON c.conference_id = s.conference_id;

text_es: Schema: Courses (course_id, course_code, course_title, credits), Prerequisites (prereq_id, course_id, required_course_id). Queries: 1. Find all direct prerequisites for a specific course. 2. List all courses that have a specific course as a prerequisite. 3. Insert a new prerequisite relationship. 4. Get all courses with no prerequisites. 5. Find courses with more than 2 prerequisites.
text_nat:
SELECT
  C.course_title,
  P.required_course_id
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Prerequisites AS P
  ON C.course_id = P.course_id
WHERE
  C.course_code = 'CS101';

SELECT
  C.course_title
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Prerequisites AS P
  ON C.course_id = P.required_course_id
WHERE
  P.required_course_id = (
    SELECT
      course_id
    FROM Courses
    WHERE
      course_code = 'MA101'
  );

INSERT INTO Prerequisites (
  course_id,
  required_course_id
)
SELECT
  C1.course_id,
  C2.course_id
FROM Courses AS C1
JOIN Courses AS C2
  ON C1.course_code = 'CS301'
  AND C2.course_code = 'CS201';

SELECT
  C.course_title
FROM Courses AS C
LEFT JOIN Prerequisites AS P
  ON C.course_id = P.course_id
WHERE
  P.prereq_id IS NULL;

SELECT
  C.course_title,
  COUNT(P.prereq_id) AS num_prerequisites
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Prerequisites AS P
  ON C.course_id = P.course_id
GROUP BY
  C.course_id,
  C.course_title
HAVING
  COUNT(P.prereq_id) > 2;

SELECT
  C.course_title,
  C.course_code
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Prerequisites AS P
  ON C.course_id = P.required_course_id;

SELECT
  C.course_title,
  P.prereq_id
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Prerequisites AS P
  ON C.course_id = P.course_id;

SELECT
  P.prereq_id,
  C.course_code
FROM Prerequisites AS P
JOIN Courses AS C
  ON P.course_id = C.course_id;

SELECT
  P.prereq_id,
  C.course_title
FROM Prerequisites AS P
JOIN Courses AS C
  ON P.required_course_id = C.course_id;

SELECT

  C2.course_title AS prerequisite
FROM Courses AS C1
JOIN Prerequisites AS P
  ON C1.course_id = P.course_id
JOIN Courses AS C2
  ON P.required_course_id = C2.course_id;

SELECT
  C.course_title,
  COUNT(P.prereq_id)

LEFT JOIN Prerequisites AS P

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username), Posts (post_id, user_id, content, posted_at), Likes (like_id, post_id, user_id, liked_at), Comments (comment_id, post_id, user_id, comment_text, commented_at). Queries: 1. Get the total number of likes for a specific post. 2. List all comments on a particular post. 3. Insert a new like for a post by a user. 4. Find posts with more than X comments. 5. Get the total engagement (likes + comments) for each post.
text_nat:
SELECT COUNT(L.like_id) AS total_likes
FROM Likes AS L
JOIN Posts AS P
ON L.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE P.post_id = 1;

SELECT C.comment_text, U.username
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Posts AS P ON C.post_id = P.post_id
JOIN Users AS U ON C.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE P.post_id = 2;

INSERT INTO Likes (post_id, user_id, liked_at)
VALUES (3, 1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);

SELECT P.post_id, P.content
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Comments AS C ON P.post_id = C.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content
HAVING COUNT(C.comment_id) > 1;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content,
       (COUNT(DISTINCT L.like_id) + COUNT(DISTINCT C.comment_id)) AS total_engagement
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Likes AS L ON P.post_id = L.post_id
LEFT JOIN Comments AS C ON P.post_id = C.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, U.username AS post_author
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Users AS U ON P.user_id = U.user_id;

SELECT L.like_id, P.content AS liked_post_content
FROM Likes AS L
JOIN Posts AS P ON L.post_id = P.post_id;

SELECT C.comment_id, U.username AS commenter_username
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Users AS U ON C.user_id = U.user_id;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, COUNT(L.like_id) AS like_count
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Likes AS L ON P.post_id = L.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, COUNT(C.comment_id) AS comment_count
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Comments AS C ON P.post_id = C.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(P.post_id) AS number_of_posts
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Posts AS P ON U.user_id = P.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(L.like_id) AS likes_given
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Likes AS L ON U.user_id = L.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(C.comment_id) AS comments_made
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Comments AS C ON U.user_id = C.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, U.username AS post_author
FROM Posts AS P
INNER JOIN Users AS U ON P.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE P.posted_at > '2023-01-01';

SELECT L.like_id, U.username AS liker_username
FROM Likes AS L
INNER JOIN Users AS U ON L.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE L.liked_at < '2023-06-30';

SELECT C.comment_id, P.content AS commented_post_content
FROM Comments AS C
INNER JOIN Posts AS P ON C.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE C.commented_at > '2023-03-01';

text_es: Schema: Vehicles (vehicle_id, make, model, year, license_plate), MaintenanceRecords (record_id, vehicle_id, service_type, service_date, cost, mileage_at_service). Queries: 1. Get all maintenance records for a specific vehicle. 2. Find the total maintenance cost for each vehicle. 3. Insert a new maintenance record. 4. Find vehicles that haven't had a specific service type in over a year. 5. List vehicles due for service based on mileage (e.g., last service at 50k, due every 10k, current mileage 59k).
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM MaintenanceRecords
JOIN Vehicles ON MaintenanceRecords.vehicle_id = Vehicles.vehicle_id
WHERE Vehicles.vehicle_id = 1;

SELECT
    v.make,
    v.model,
    SUM(mr.cost) AS total_maintenance_cost
FROM Vehicles AS v
JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
GROUP BY
    v.make,
    v.model;

INSERT INTO MaintenanceRecords (vehicle_id, service_type, service_date, cost, mileage_at_service)
VALUES (1, 'Oil Change', '2023-10-26', 75.00, 65000);

SELECT v.make, v.model
FROM Vehicles AS v
LEFT JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
WHERE mr.service_type = 'Tire Rotation'
  AND mr.service_date < DATE('now', '-1 year')
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id
HAVING COUNT(mr.record_id) = 1;

SELECT
    v.make,
    v.model,
    v.license_plate
FROM Vehicles AS v
JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
WHERE mr.service_type = 'Oil Change'
  AND mr.service_date = (
    SELECT MAX(mr2.service_date)
    FROM MaintenanceRecords AS mr2
    WHERE mr2.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
      AND mr2.service_type = 'Oil Change'
  )
  AND mr.mileage_at_service + 10000 < 59000;

SELECT v.make, v.model
FROM Vehicles AS v
JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
WHERE mr.service_type = 'Brake Inspection';

SELECT mr.service_type, COUNT(v.vehicle_id)

JOIN Users u ON b.reporter_id = u.user_id;

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name), Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd). Queries: 1. Get the current price for a specific product. 2. List the full pricing history for a product. 3. Insert a new price for a product (new effective date). 4. Find products whose price has increased in the last year. 5. Get the latest price for all products.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Prices (
    price_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id INT,
    effective_date DATE,
    price_usd DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

-- Query 1: Get the current price for a specific product
SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_name = 'Laptop'
  AND pr.effective_date = (
    SELECT MAX(effective_date)
    FROM Prices
    WHERE product_id = p.product_id
  );

-- Query 2: List the full pricing history for a product
SELECT pr.effective_date, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_name = 'Laptop'
ORDER BY pr.effective_date DESC;

-- Query 3: Insert a new price for a product (new effective date)
INSERT INTO Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd)
VALUES (4, (SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE product_name = 'Laptop'), '2024-03-01', 1250.00);

-- Query 4: Find products whose price has increased in the last year
SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr1
  ON p.product_id = pr1.product_id
JOIN Prices pr2
  ON p.product_id = pr2.product_id
WHERE pr1.effective_date >= DATE('now', '-1 year')
  AND pr2.effective_date >= DATE('now', '-1 year')
  AND pr1.effective_date < pr2.effective_date
  AND pr2.price_usd > pr1.price_usd;

-- Query 5: Get the latest price for all products
SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE pr.effective_date = (
    SELECT MAX(effective_date)
    FROM Prices
    WHERE product_id = p.product_id
);

-- Additional queries with exactly ONE join between two tables

SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE pr.price_usd > 1000;

SELECT pr.price_id, pr.effective_date
FROM Prices pr
JOIN Products p
  ON pr.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.product_name = 'Keyboard';

SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
ORDER BY pr.price_usd DESC;

SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE pr.effective_date < '2023-01-01';

SELECT pr.price_id, p.product_name
FROM Prices pr
JOIN Products p
  ON pr.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE pr.price_usd < 50;

SELECT p.product_id, pr.effective_date
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_name LIKE 'M%';

SELECT pr.price_usd, p.product_name
FROM Prices pr
JOIN Products p
  ON pr.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY p.product_name ASC;

SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id
HAVING COUNT(pr.price_id) > 1;

text_es: Schema: Departments (dept_id, dept_name, budget_total), Expenses (expense_id, dept_id, expense_date, amount, description). Queries: 1. Get the total expenses for a specific department. 2. List all expenses for a department in a given month. 3. Insert a new expense record. 4. Find departments that are over budget. 5. Get the remaining budget for each department.
text_nat:
SELECT SUM(E.amount)
FROM Expenses AS E
JOIN Departments AS D
ON E.dept_id = D.dept_id
WHERE D.dept_name = 'Marketing';

SELECT E.expense_id, E.expense_date, E.amount, E.description
FROM Expenses AS E
JOIN Departments AS D
ON E.dept_id = D.dept_id
WHERE D.dept_name = 'Sales' AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', E.expense_date) = '2023-01';

INSERT INTO Expenses (dept_id, expense_date, amount, description)
VALUES (1, '2023-03-15', 150.00, 'Office Supplies');

SELECT D.dept_name, D.budget_total, SUM(E.amount) AS total_expenses
FROM Departments AS D
JOIN Expenses AS E

text_es: Schema: Agents (agent_id, agent_name, department), Tickets (ticket_id, agent_id, customer_id, opened_at, closed_at, status, resolution_notes). Queries: 1. Get the number of tickets closed by a specific agent. 2. List all open tickets assigned to an agent. 3. Assign a ticket to an agent. 4. Close a ticket with resolution notes. 5. Find agents with an average resolution time longer than X hours.
text_nat:
SELECT COUNT(T.ticket_id)
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Agents AS A ON T.agent_id = A.agent_id
WHERE A.agent_name = 'Alice Smith' AND T.status = 'Closed';

SELECT T.ticket_id, T.opened_at
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Agents AS A ON T.agent_id = A.agent_id
WHERE A.agent_name = 'Bob Johnson' AND T.status = 'Open';

UPDATE Tickets
SET agent_id = (SELECT agent_id FROM Agents WHERE agent_name = 'Charlie Brown')
WHERE ticket_id = 101;

UPDATE Tickets
SET status = 'Closed', closed_at = NOW(), resolution_notes = 'Issue resolved after troubleshooting.'
WHERE ticket_id = 102;

SELECT A.agent_name,
       AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (T.closed_at - T.opened_at))) / 3600 AS avg_resolution_hours
FROM Agents AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T ON A.agent_id = T.agent_id
WHERE T.status = 'Closed'
GROUP BY A.agent_name
HAVING AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (T.closed_at - T.opened_at))) / 3600 > 24;

SELECT T.ticket_id, T.opened_at, T.status, A.agent_name
FROM Tickets AS T

List all tasks for a specific project. 2. Find all tasks that a specific task depends on. 3. Insert a new task dependency. 4. Find tasks that are 'pending' but have all their dependencies 'completed'. 5. Get the count of dependencies for each task.

SELECT *
FROM Tasks
JOIN Projects ON Tasks.project_id = Projects.project_id
WHERE Projects.project_name = 'Alpha Project';

SELECT T1.task_name AS task, T2.task_name AS depends_on
FROM TaskDependencies TD

JOIN Tasks T2 ON TD.depends_on_task_id = T2.task_id
WHERE T1.task_name = 'Develop UI';

SELECT T.task_name
FROM Tasks T
JOIN TaskDependencies TD ON T.task_id = TD.task_id

AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM TaskDependencies TD2
    JOIN Tasks T2 ON TD2.depends_on_task_id = T2.task_id
    WHERE TD2.task_id = T.task_id AND T2.status != 'completed'
);

SELECT T.task_name, COUNT(TD.depends_on_task_id) AS dependency_count

GROUP BY T.task_name;

text_es: Schema: Courses (course_id, course_title), Modules (module_id, course_id, module_title, order_index), Lessons (lesson_id, module_id, lesson_title, lesson_type, duration_minutes). Queries: 1. List all modules for a specific course, ordered. 2. Find all lessons within a particular module. 3. Insert a new lesson into a module. 4. Update the order index of a module. 5. Get the total duration of lessons per module.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Courses (
    course_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    course_title VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Modules (
    module_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    course_id INT,
    module_title VARCHAR(255),
    order_index INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES Courses(course_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Lessons (
    lesson_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    module_id INT,
    lesson_title VARCHAR(255),
    lesson_type VARCHAR(50),
    duration_minutes INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (module_id) REFERENCES Modules(module_id)
);

INSERT INTO Courses (course_id, course_title) VALUES

INSERT INTO Lessons (lesson_id, module_id, lesson_title, lesson_type, duration_minutes) VALUES

(5, 201, 'Subqueries', 'Video', 30);

-- Query 1: List all modules for a specific course, ordered.
SELECT M.module_id, M.module_title
FROM Modules AS M
JOIN Courses AS C ON M.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE C.course_id = 1
ORDER BY M.order_index;

-- Query 2: Find all lessons within a particular module.
SELECT L.lesson_id, L.lesson_title
FROM Lessons AS L
JOIN Modules AS M ON L.module_id = M.module_id
WHERE M.module_id = 101;

-- Query 3: Insert a new lesson into a module.
INSERT INTO Lessons (lesson_id, module_id, lesson_title, lesson_type, duration_minutes)
VALUES (6, 102, 'JOINs explained', 'Video', 35);

-- Query 4: Update the order index of a module.
UPDATE Modules
SET order_index = 3
WHERE module_id = 102;

-- Query 5: Get the total duration of lessons per module.
SELECT M.module_title, SUM(L.duration_minutes) AS total_duration
FROM Modules AS M
JOIN Lessons AS L ON M.module_id = L.module_id
GROUP BY M.module_title;

SELECT C.course_title, M.module_title
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Modules AS M ON C.course_id = M.course_id;

SELECT M.module_title, L.lesson_title
FROM Modules AS M
JOIN Lessons AS L ON M.module_id = L.module_id;

SELECT C.course_title, L.lesson_title
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Modules AS M ON C.course_id = M.course_id
JOIN Lessons AS L ON M.module_id = L.module_id;

SELECT C.course_title, M.module_title, L.lesson_title, L.duration_minutes
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Modules AS M ON C.course_id = M.course_id
JOIN Lessons AS L ON M.module_id = L.module_id
WHERE C.course_id = 1 AND L.lesson_type = 'Video';

SELECT L.lesson_title, L.duration_minutes
FROM Lessons AS L
JOIN Modules AS M ON L.module_id = M.module_id
WHERE M.module_id = 101;

SELECT M.module_title, COUNT(L.lesson_id) AS number_of_lessons
FROM Modules AS M
JOIN Lessons AS L ON M.module_id = L.module_id
GROUP BY M.module_title;

SELECT C.course_title, M.module_title
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Modules AS M ON C.course_id = M.course_id
ORDER BY C.course_title, M.order_index;

SELECT L.lesson_title, M.module_title
FROM Lessons AS L
JOIN Modules AS M ON L.module_id = M.module_id
WHERE L.duration_minutes > 20;

SELECT C.course_title, SUM(L.duration_minutes) AS total_course_duration
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Modules AS M ON C.course_id = M.course_id
JOIN Lessons AS L ON M.module_id = L.module_id
GROUP BY C.course_title;

text_es: Schema: Events (event_id, event_name, event_date), Attendees (attendee_id, event_id, first_name, last_name, company, badge_printed). Queries: 1. List all attendees for a specific event. 2. Find all attendees from a particular company for an event. 3. Mark an attendee's badge as 'printed'. 4. Insert a new attendee for an event. 5. Get the count of attendees whose badges have not been printed.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Events (
    event_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_name VARCHAR(255),
    event_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Attendees (
    attendee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_id INT,
    first_name VARCHAR(255),
    last_name VARCHAR(255),
    company VARCHAR(255),
    badge_printed BOOLEAN
);

INSERT INTO Events (event_id, event_name, event_date) VALUES
(1, 'Tech Conference 2023', '2023-10-26'),
(2, 'Marketing Summit', '2023-11-15');

INSERT INTO Attendees (attendee_id, event_id, first_name, last_name, company, badge_printed) VALUES
(101, 1, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'Innovate Corp', FALSE),
(102, 1, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'Innovate Corp', TRUE),
(103, 1, 'Charlie', 'Brown', 'Global Solutions', FALSE),
(104, 2, 'Diana', 'Prince', 'Wonder Co', TRUE),
(105, 2, 'Eve', 'Adams', 'Innovate Corp', FALSE);

-- Query 1: List all attendees for a specific event (e.g., event_id = 1)
SELECT A.first_name, A.last_name, E.event_name
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_id = 1;

-- Query 2: Find all attendees from a particular company for an event (e.g., event_id = 1, company = 'Innovate Corp')
SELECT A.first_name, A.last_name, A.company, E.event_name
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_id = 1 AND A.company = 'Innovate Corp';

-- Query 3: Mark an attendee's badge as 'printed' (e.g., attendee_id = 101)
UPDATE Attendees
SET badge_printed = TRUE
WHERE attendee_id = 101;

-- Query 4: Insert a new attendee for an event (e.g., event_id = 1)
INSERT INTO Attendees (attendee_id, event_id, first_name, last_name, company, badge_printed)
VALUES (106, 1, 'Frank', 'Green', 'Global Solutions', FALSE);

-- Query 5: Get the count of attendees whose badges have not been printed
SELECT COUNT(A.attendee_id)
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE A.badge_printed = FALSE;

-- Additional queries with exactly one join
SELECT A.first_name, A.last_name
FROM Attendees AS A JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id;

SELECT E.event_name, A.company
FROM Events AS E JOIN Attendees AS A ON E.event_id = A.event_id;

SELECT A.attendee_id, E.event_name
FROM Attendees AS A JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE A.badge_printed = TRUE;

SELECT A.first_name, E.event_date
FROM Attendees AS A JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_date = '2023-10-26';

SELECT E.event_id, COUNT(A.attendee_id)
FROM Events AS E JOIN Attendees AS A ON E.event_id = A.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_id;

SELECT A.first_name, A.last_name
FROM Attendees AS A JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_name = 'Marketing Summit';

SELECT A.company, E.event_name
FROM Attendees AS A JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
GROUP BY A.company, E.event_name;

SELECT A.first_name, A.last_name
FROM Attendees AS A JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
ORDER BY E.event_date DESC;

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username, email), NotificationTypes (type_id, type_name, description), UserPreferences (user_id, type_id, enabled). Queries: 1. Get all notification preferences for a specific user. 2. Find all users who have a specific notification type enabled. 3. Update a user's preference for a notification type. 4. Find all notification types that are enabled by default (i.e., not in UserPreferences with enabled=false). 5. Count users who have opted out of a specific notification type.
text_nat:
SELECT U.username, NP.type_name, UP.enabled
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
ON U.user_id = UP.user_id
JOIN NotificationTypes AS NP
ON UP.type_id = NP.type_id
WHERE U.username = 'john_doe';

SELECT U.username, U.email
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
ON U.user_id = UP.user_id
JOIN NotificationTypes AS NT
ON UP.type_id = NT.type_id
WHERE NT.type_name = 'Email Updates' AND UP.enabled = TRUE;

UPDATE UserPreferences
SET enabled = FALSE
WHERE user_id = (SELECT user_id FROM Users WHERE username = 'john_doe')
AND type_id = (SELECT type_id FROM NotificationTypes WHERE type_name = 'SMS Alerts');

SELECT NT.type_name, NT.description
FROM NotificationTypes AS NT
LEFT JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
ON NT.type_id = UP.type_id
WHERE UP.enabled IS NULL OR UP.enabled = TRUE;

SELECT U.username, U.email
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
ON U.user_id = UP.user_id;

SELECT NT.type_name, NT.description
FROM NotificationTypes AS NT

ON NT.type_id = UP.type_id
WHERE UP.enabled = FALSE;

FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
ON U.user_id = UP.user_id
JOIN NotificationTypes AS NT
ON UP.type_id = NT.type_id

text_es: Schema: Assets (asset_id, asset_tag, asset_type, purchase_date, cost), Locations (location_id, location_name), AssetLocations (asset_id, location_id, assigned_date, released_date). Queries: 1. Get the current location of a specific asset. 2. List all assets at a particular location. 3. Assign an asset to a new location (end old assignment, start new). 4. Find assets purchased before a specific date. 5. Get the total cost of assets per asset type.
text_nat:
SELECT A.asset_tag, L.location_name
FROM Assets AS A
JOIN AssetLocations AS AL ON A.asset_id = AL.asset_id
JOIN Locations AS L ON AL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE A.asset_id = 1 AND AL.released_date IS NULL;

SELECT A.asset_tag, A.asset_type
FROM Assets AS A
JOIN AssetLocations AS AL ON A.asset_id = AL.asset_id
JOIN Locations AS L ON AL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE L.location_name = 'Warehouse A' AND AL.released_date IS NULL;

UPDATE AssetLocations
SET released_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE asset_id = 1 AND released_date IS NULL;

text_es: Schema: Posts (post_id, content, user_id, posted_at), Reactions (reaction_id, post_id, user_id, reaction_type, reacted_at). Queries: 1. Get the total count of a specific reaction type for a post. 2. List all users who reacted to a particular post. 3. Insert a new reaction to a post. 4. Find posts with more than 10 'like' reactions. 5. Get the total number of unique users who reacted to each post.
text_nat:
SELECT COUNT(R.reaction_id) AS total_likes
FROM Reactions AS R
JOIN Posts AS P
ON R.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE R.post_id = 123 AND R.reaction_type = 'like';

SELECT DISTINCT U.user_id, U.username
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Reactions AS R
ON U.user_id = R.user_id
WHERE R.post_id = 456;

INSERT INTO Reactions (post_id, user_id, reaction_type, reacted_at)
VALUES (789, 101, 'heart', NOW());

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, COUNT(R.reaction_id) AS like_count
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Reactions AS R
ON P.post_id = R.post_id
WHERE R.reaction_type = 'like'
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content
HAVING COUNT(R.reaction_id) > 10;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, COUNT(DISTINCT R.user_id) AS unique_reactors
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Reactions AS R
ON P.post_id = R.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

SELECT R.reaction_id, R.reaction_type
FROM Reactions AS R
JOIN Posts AS P
ON R.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE P.post_id = 555;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Reactions AS R
ON P.post_id = R.post_id
WHERE R.reaction_id IS NULL;

SELECT U.user_id, U.username
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Posts AS P
ON U.user_id = P.user_id
WHERE P.post_id = 999;

SELECT R.user_id, COUNT(R.reaction_id) AS total_reactions
FROM Reactions AS R
JOIN Users AS U
ON R.user_id = U.user_id
GROUP BY R.user_id;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Reactions AS R
ON P.post_id = R.post_id
WHERE R.reaction_type = 'angry';

SELECT P.post_id, COUNT(R.reaction_id)
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Reactions AS R
ON P.post_id = R.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id
ORDER BY COUNT(R.reaction_id) DESC;

SELECT U.user_id, U.username
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Reactions AS R
ON U.user_id = R.user_id
WHERE R.reaction_type = 'laugh';

SELECT P.post_id, P.content

ON P.post_id = R.post_id
WHERE R.user_id = 202;

List all returns made by a specific customer. 2. Find all returns for a particular product. 3. Insert a new product return record. 4. Get the total refund amount for each customer. 5. Find products with more than 10 returns in the last month.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Returns
JOIN Customers ON Returns.customer_id = Customers.customer_id
WHERE Customers.customer_name = 'Alice Smith';

SELECT R.return_id, P.product_name, R.return_date
FROM Returns AS R
JOIN Products AS P ON R.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE P.product_name = 'Laptop';

VALUES (101, 1, 3, '2023-11-01', 'Defective', 120.00);

FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Returns AS R ON C.customer_id = R.customer_id
GROUP BY C.customer_name;

SELECT P.product_name, COUNT(R.return_id) AS total_returns
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Returns AS R ON P.product_id = R.product_id
WHERE R.return_date >= DATE('now', '-1 month')
GROUP BY P.product_name
HAVING COUNT(R.return_id) > 10;

JOIN Returns AS R ON P.product_id = R.product_id
JOIN Customers AS C ON R.customer_id = C.customer_id;

JOIN Returns AS R ON C.customer_id = R.customer_id
JOIN Products AS P ON R.product_id = P.product_id

SELECT R.return_id, P.product_name

ON C.customer_id = R.customer_id;

JOIN Employees AS E ON R.reviewer_id = E.employee_id

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username), Events (event_id, event_name, description), UserEvents (user_event_id, user_id, event_id, event_timestamp, event_data). Queries: 1. List all events performed by a specific user. 2. Find the total occurrences of a particular event. 3. Insert a new user event. 4. Get the top 5 most frequent events. 5. Count unique users who performed each event.
text_nat:
SELECT E.event_name, E.description
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
WHERE UE.user_id = 1;

SELECT event_name, COUNT(*) AS total_occurrences
FROM Events
JOIN UserEvents ON Events.event_id = UserEvents.event_id
WHERE Events.event_name = 'User Login'
GROUP BY event_name;

INSERT INTO UserEvents (user_id, event_id, event_timestamp, event_data)
VALUES (2, 3, '2023-10-27 10:00:00', '{"ip_address": "192.168.1.1"}');

SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(UE.event_id) AS event_count
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_name
ORDER BY event_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(DISTINCT UE.user_id) AS unique_users
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_name;

SELECT U.username, E.event_name
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON U.user_id = UE.user_id
JOIN Events AS E ON UE.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE U.user_id = 1
ORDER BY E.event_name;

SELECT U.username
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON U.user_id = UE.user_id
GROUP BY U.username
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT UE.event_id) > 2;

SELECT E.event_name, UE.event_timestamp
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
WHERE E.event_name = 'Page View'
ORDER BY UE.event_timestamp DESC
LIMIT 10;

SELECT U.username, E.event_name, UE.event_timestamp
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON U.user_id = UE.user_id
JOIN Events AS E ON UE.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE UE.event_timestamp BETWEEN '2023-10-26' AND '2023-10-27'
ORDER BY UE.event_timestamp;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(UE.event_id) AS total_events
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON U.user_id = UE.user_id
GROUP BY U.username
ORDER BY total_events DESC
LIMIT 3;

SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(UE.user_id)
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_name;

SELECT U.username
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON U.user_id = UE.user_id
WHERE UE.event_id = 1;
text_alt:

FROM Events AS E, UserEvents AS UE
WHERE E.event_id = UE.event_id
AND UE.user_id = 1;

SELECT event_name, COUNT(*) AS total_occurrences

WHERE Events.event_id = UserEvents.event_id
AND Events.event_name = 'User Login'

INSERT INTO UserEvents (user_id, event_id, event_timestamp, event_data)
VALUES (2, 3, '2023-10-27 10:00:00', '{"ip_address": "192.168.1.1"}');

FROM Events AS E, UserEvents AS UE
WHERE E.event_id = UE.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_name
ORDER BY event_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(DISTINCT UE.user_id) AS unique_users
FROM Events AS E, UserEvents AS UE
WHERE E.event_id = UE.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_name;

SELECT U.username, E.event_name
FROM Users AS U, UserEvents AS UE, Events AS E
WHERE U.user_id = UE.user_id
AND UE.event_id = E.event_id
AND U.user_id = 1
ORDER BY E.event_name;

SELECT U.username
FROM Users AS U, UserEvents AS UE
WHERE U.user_id = UE.user_id
GROUP BY U.username
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT UE.event_id) > 2;

SELECT E.event_name, UE.event_timestamp
FROM Events AS E, UserEvents AS UE
WHERE E.event_id = UE.event_id
AND E.event_name = 'Page View'
ORDER BY UE.event_timestamp DESC
LIMIT 10;

SELECT U.username, E.event_name, UE.event_timestamp
FROM Users AS U, UserEvents AS UE, Events AS E
WHERE U.user_id = UE.user_id
AND UE.event_id = E.event_id

WHERE U.user_id = UE.user_id

LIMIT 3;

SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(UE.user_id)

text_es: Schema: Providers (provider_id, provider_name, specialty), Certifications (cert_id, cert_name, issuing_body), ProviderCertifications (provider_id, cert_id, issue_date, expiry_date). Queries: 1. List all certifications held by a specific provider. 2. Find all providers with a particular certification. 3. Insert a new certification for a provider. 4. Find providers whose certifications are expiring in the next 90 days. 5. Get the count of providers per specialty.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Providers (
    provider_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    provider_name VARCHAR(255),
    specialty VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Certifications (
    cert_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    cert_name VARCHAR(255),
    issuing_body VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE ProviderCertifications (
    provider_id INT,
    cert_id INT,
    issue_date DATE,
    expiry_date DATE,
    PRIMARY KEY (provider_id, cert_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES Providers(provider_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (cert_id) REFERENCES Certifications(cert_id)
);

-- Query 1: List all certifications held by a specific provider (e.g., provider_id = 1)
SELECT
    C.cert_name,
    PC.issue_date,
    PC.expiry_date
FROM
    Certifications AS C
JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
    ON C.cert_id = PC.cert_id
WHERE
    PC.provider_id = 1;

-- Query 2: Find all providers with a particular certification (e.g., cert_id = 101)
SELECT
    P.provider_name,
    P.specialty
FROM
    Providers AS P
JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
    ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
WHERE
    PC.cert_id = 101;

-- Query 3: Insert a new certification for a provider (e.g., provider_id = 2, cert_id = 103, dates)
INSERT INTO ProviderCertifications (provider_id, cert_id, issue_date, expiry_date)
VALUES (2, 103, '2023-01-15', '2025-01-14');

-- Query 4: Find providers whose certifications are expiring in the next 90 days
SELECT
    P.provider_name,
    C.cert_name,
    PC.expiry_date
FROM
    Providers AS P
JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
    ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
JOIN Certifications AS C
    ON PC.cert_id = C.cert_id
WHERE
    PC.expiry_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 90 DAY);

-- Query 5: Get the count of providers per specialty
SELECT
    specialty,
    COUNT(provider_id) AS provider_count
FROM
    Providers
GROUP BY
    specialty;

-- Additional queries with exactly one join
SELECT P.provider_name, PC.issue_date
FROM Providers AS P JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id;

SELECT C.cert_name, PC.expiry_date

ON C.cert_id = PC.cert_id;

text_es: Schema: Employees (employee_id, employee_name, manager_id), TimeOffTypes (type_id, type_name), TimeOffRequests (request_id, employee_id, type_id, start_date, end_date, status, approved_by_manager_id). Queries: 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee. 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager. 3. Submit a new time off request. 4. Approve a time off request. 5. Get the total number of days requested per time off type.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee.
SELECT
    TOR.request_id,
    E.employee_name,
    TOT.type_name,
    TOR.start_date,
    TOR.end_date
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON TOR.employee_id = E.employee_id
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
WHERE
    E.employee_id = 101 AND TOR.status = 'Pending';

-- 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager.
SELECT
    TOR.request_id,
    Emp.employee_name AS employee_requesting,
    Mgr.employee_name AS manager_to_approve,
    TOT.type_name,
    TOR.start_date,
    TOR.end_date
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    Employees AS Emp ON TOR.employee_id = Emp.employee_id
JOIN
    Employees AS Mgr ON Emp.manager_id = Mgr.employee_id
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
WHERE
    Mgr.employee_id = 201 AND TOR.status = 'Pending';

-- Single join queries below

SELECT R.request_id, R.start_date
FROM TimeOffRequests AS R
JOIN Employees AS E ON R.employee_id = E.employee_id;

SELECT T.type_name, T.type_id
FROM TimeOffTypes AS T
JOIN TimeOffRequests AS R ON T.type_id = R.type_id;

SELECT E.employee_name, M.employee_name AS manager_name
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN Employees AS M ON E.manager_id = M.employee_id;

-- 3. Submit a new time off request.
INSERT INTO TimeOffRequests (employee_id, type_id, start_date, end_date, status)
VALUES (101, 1, '2023-12-25', '2023-12-26', 'Pending');

-- 4. Approve a time off request.
UPDATE TimeOffRequests
SET status = 'Approved', approved_by_manager_id = 201
WHERE request_id = 1;

SELECT R.request_id, E.employee_name
FROM TimeOffRequests AS R
JOIN Employees AS E ON R.approved_by_manager_id = E.employee_id;

SELECT E.employee_name, R.status
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN TimeOffRequests AS R ON E.employee_id = R.employee_id;

-- 5. Get the total number of days requested per time off type.
SELECT
    TOT.type_name,
    SUM(JULIANDAY(TOR.end_date) - JULIANDAY(TOR.start_date) + 1) AS total_days_requested
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
GROUP BY
    TOT.type_name;

SELECT T.type_name, R.start_date
FROM TimeOffTypes AS T
JOIN TimeOffRequests AS R ON T.type_id = R.type_id;

SELECT E.employee_name, R.request_id
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN TimeOffRequests AS R ON E.employee_id = R.employee_id;

text_es: Schema: Articles (article_id, title, content, author_id, publish_date), Categories (category_id, category_name), ArticleCategories (article_id, category_id). Queries: 1. Find all articles in a specific category. 2. List all categories an article belongs to. 3. Insert a new article and assign it to a category. 4. Find articles containing a specific keyword in their title or content. 5. Get the count of articles per category.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all articles in a specific category (e.g., 'Technology')
SELECT
    A.title,
    A.publish_date
FROM
    Articles AS A
JOIN
    ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id
JOIN
    Categories AS C ON AC.category_id = C.category_id
WHERE
    C.category_name = 'Technology';

-- 2. List all categories an article belongs to (e.g., article_id = 1)
SELECT
    C.category_name
FROM
    Categories AS C
JOIN
    ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id
WHERE
    AC.article_id = 1;

-- 3. Insert a new article and assign it to a category
INSERT INTO Articles (article_id, title, content, author_id, publish_date)
VALUES (101, 'New Article Title', 'Content of the new article.', 5, '2023-10-26');

INSERT INTO ArticleCategories (article_id, category_id)
VALUES (101, (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Science'));

-- 4. Find articles containing a specific keyword in their title or content (e.g., 'database')
SELECT
    A.title,
    A.content
FROM
    Articles AS A
WHERE
    A.title LIKE '%database%' OR A.content LIKE '%database%';

-- 5. Get the count of articles per category
SELECT
    C.category_name,
    COUNT(A.article_id) AS article_count
FROM
    Categories AS C
LEFT JOIN
    ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id
LEFT JOIN
    Articles AS A ON AC.article_id = A.article_id
GROUP BY
    C.category_name;

-- Separate queries, each with exactly ONE join between two tables

SELECT A.title FROM Articles AS A JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id;
SELECT C.category_name FROM Categories AS C JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id;

SELECT COUNT(A.article_id) FROM Articles AS A JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id;

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name, base_price), Variants (variant_id, product_id, color, size, sku, stock_quantity, additional_cost). Queries: 1. List all variants for a specific product. 2. Find all products that have a variant with a specific color. 3. Update the stock quantity for a variant. 4. Get the full price (base_price + additional_cost) for each variant. 5. Find products with no variants currently in stock.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255),
    base_price DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Variants (
    variant_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id INT,
    color VARCHAR(50),
    size VARCHAR(50),
    sku VARCHAR(100),
    stock_quantity INT,
    additional_cost DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

INSERT INTO Products (product_id, product_name, base_price) VALUES
(1, 'T-Shirt', 15.00),
(2, 'Jeans', 45.00),
(3, 'Socks', 5.00);

INSERT INTO Variants (variant_id, product_id, color, size, sku, stock_quantity, additional_cost) VALUES
(101, 1, 'Red', 'M', 'TS-RD-M', 10, 2.00),
(102, 1, 'Blue', 'L', 'TS-BL-L', 5, 2.50),
(103, 2, 'Blue', '32', 'JN-BL-32', 8, 5.00),
(104, 2, 'Black', '34', 'JN-BK-34', 0, 6.00),
(105, 3, 'White', 'One Size', 'SK-WH-OS', 20, 0.50);

-- Query 1: List all variants for a specific product (e.g., product_id = 1)
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    v.color,
    v.size,
    v.stock_quantity
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id
WHERE p.product_id = 1;

-- Query 2: Find all products that have a variant with a specific color (e.g., 'Blue')
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.product_name
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id
WHERE v.color = 'Blue';

-- Query 3: Update the stock quantity for a variant (e.g., variant_id = 102 to 7)
UPDATE Variants
SET stock_quantity = 7
WHERE variant_id = 102;

-- Query 4: Get the full price (base_price + additional_cost) for each variant
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    v.color,
    v.size,
    (p.base_price + v.additional_cost) AS full_price
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id;

-- Query 5: Find products with no variants currently in stock
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.product_name
FROM
    Products AS p
LEFT JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING SUM(v.stock_quantity) = 0 OR COUNT(v.variant_id) = 0;

-- Additional queries with single JOINs, each on its own line
SELECT product_name, color, size FROM Products JOIN Variants ON Products.product_id = Variants.product_id;

SELECT product_name, stock_quantity FROM Products JOIN Variants ON Products.product_id = Variants.product_id WHERE color = 'Red';

SELECT variant_id, sku, product_name FROM Variants JOIN Products ON Variants.product_id = Products.product_id;

SELECT p.product_name, v.color FROM Products AS p JOIN Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id WHERE v.size = 'M';

SELECT p.product_name, v.sku FROM Products AS p JOIN Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id ORDER BY p.product_name;

SELECT v.variant_id, p.base_price FROM Variants AS v JOIN Products AS p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE v.stock_quantity > 5;

SELECT p.product_name FROM Products AS p JOIN Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id WHERE v.additional_cost > 3.00;

SELECT v.color FROM Variants AS v JOIN Products AS p ON v.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY v.color HAVING COUNT(p.product_id) > 1;

Schema: Documents (doc_id INT, title VARCHAR, content TEXT, created_at DATETIME, author_id INT), Authors (author_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Select all documents created by a specific author.
2. Find the total number of documents for each author.
3. Insert a new document.
4. Update the content of an existing document.
5. Select the 5 most recent documents.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Authors (
    author_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Documents (
    doc_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    content TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME,
    author_id INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (author_id) REFERENCES Authors(author_id)
);

-- Insert sample data
INSERT INTO Authors (author_id, name, email) VALUES
(1, 'Alice Smith', 'alice@example.com'),
(2, 'Bob Johnson', 'bob@example.com');

INSERT INTO Documents (doc_id, title, content, created_at, author_id) VALUES
(101, 'My First Post', 'This is the content of my first post.', '2023-01-01 10:00:00', 1),
(102, 'Database Design', 'Details about database design.', '2023-01-02 11:00:00', 2),
(103, 'SQL Joins', 'Understanding different types of SQL joins.', '2023-01-03 12:00:00', 1),
(104, 'New Tech Trends', 'Exploring the latest tech trends.', '2023-01-04 13:00:00', 2),
(105, 'Advanced SQL', 'Advanced SQL concepts and queries.', '2023-01-05 14:00:00', 1);

-- 1. Select all documents created by a specific author (e.g., 'Alice Smith')
SELECT D.title, D.content
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.name = 'Alice Smith';

-- 2. Find the total number of documents for each author.
SELECT A.name, COUNT(D.doc_id) AS total_documents
FROM Authors AS A
JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
GROUP BY A.name;

-- 3. Insert a new document
INSERT INTO Documents (doc_id, title, content, created_at, author_id)
VALUES (106, 'Another Document', 'Content for another document.', '2023-01-06 15:00:00', 2);

-- 4. Update the content of an existing document
UPDATE Documents
SET content = 'Updated content for My First Post.'
WHERE doc_id = 101;

-- 5. Select the 5 most recent documents.
SELECT doc_id, title, created_at
FROM Documents
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- SEPARATE QUERIES WITH EXACTLY ONE JOIN

-- Select document titles and author emails
SELECT D.title, A.email
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id;

-- Get author names and their document titles, even if no documents
SELECT A.name, D.title
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id;

-- Get documents and author names for specific document ID
SELECT D.title, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE D.doc_id = 103;

-- List all authors and the count of their documents
SELECT A.name, COUNT(D.doc_id)
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
GROUP BY A.name;

-- Get document creation dates and author names
SELECT D.created_at, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id;

-- Select documents whose author's email ends with 'example.com'
SELECT D.title, A.email
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.email LIKE '%@example.com';

-- Find documents written by authors whose name starts with 'B'
SELECT D.title, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.name LIKE 'B%';

-- Retrieve author names and the titles of documents they published after '2023-01-03'
SELECT A.name, D.title
FROM Authors AS A
JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
WHERE D.created_at > '2023-01-03';

Schema: Products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR, description TEXT, price DECIMAL), Warehouses (warehouse_id INT, location VARCHAR, capacity INT), Inventory (product_id INT, warehouse_id INT, quantity INT, last_updated DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all products in a specific warehouse with quantity greater than 100.
2. Calculate the total quantity of a given product across all warehouses.
3. Add a new product to a warehouse's inventory.
4. Decrease the quantity of a product in a warehouse.
5. List all warehouses and the number of distinct products they store.
text_nat:
SELECT P.name, P.description, P.price
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Inventory AS I
ON P.product_id = I.product_id
WHERE I.warehouse_id = 1 AND I.quantity > 100;

FROM Inventory AS I
JOIN Products AS P
ON I.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE P.name = 'Laptop';

    (SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE name = 'Keyboard'),
    (SELECT warehouse_id FROM Warehouses WHERE location = 'New York'),

    NOW()
);

WHERE product_id = (SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE name = 'Mouse')
AND warehouse_id = (SELECT warehouse_id FROM Warehouses WHERE location = 'New York');

FROM Warehouses AS W
JOIN Inventory AS I

ON P.product_id = I.product_id;

WHERE I.product_id IS NULL;

JOIN Events AS E

Queries:

5. Count the number of students per department.

(3, 2, 101, 'C');

-- 1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in (e.g., student_id = 1)
SELECT C.title, C.department
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. List all students enrolled in a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101)
SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id
WHERE E.course_id = 101;

INSERT INTO Enrollments (enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, grade)
VALUES (4, 3, 103, NULL);

SET grade = 'B+'
WHERE student_id = 2 AND course_id = 101;

-- 5. Count the number of students per department.
SELECT C.department, COUNT(DISTINCT E.student_id) AS number_of_students
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
GROUP BY C.department;

Schema: Recipes (recipe_id INT, name VARCHAR, instructions TEXT, cook_time_minutes INT), Ingredients (ingredient_id INT, name VARCHAR, unit VARCHAR), RecipeIngredients (recipe_id INT, ingredient_id INT, quantity DECIMAL).
Queries:
1. Find all ingredients for a specific recipe.
2. List all recipes that use a particular ingredient.
3. Add a new ingredient to a recipe.
4. Update the cook time of a recipe.

SELECT
    I.name AS ingredient_name,
    RI.quantity,
    I.unit
FROM
    Recipes R JOIN RecipeIngredients RI

JOIN
    Ingredients I ON RI.ingredient_id = I.ingredient_id
WHERE
    R.name = 'Spaghetti Carbonara';

    R.cook_time_minutes
FROM
    Recipes R JOIN RecipeIngredients RI

WHERE
    I.name = 'Garlic';

    R.recipe_id,
    I.ingredient_id,
    2.5
FROM

    ON R.name = 'Chicken Stir-Fry' AND I.name = 'Soy Sauce';

UPDATE Recipes
SET cook_time_minutes = 45
WHERE name = 'Beef Stew';

Queries:
1. Find all bugs assigned to a specific user with 'High' priority.
2. List all bugs with status 'Open' or 'Reopened'.
3. Create a new bug report.
4. Update a bug's status to 'Closed'.
5. Count the number of bugs per status.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Bugs (bug_id, title, description, status, priority, created_at, assigned_to)
VALUES (101, 'Login failure', 'Users cannot log in', 'Open', 'High', NOW(), 'john.doe');

SET status = 'Closed'
WHERE bug_id = 101;

SELECT
    b.bug_id,
    b.title,
    b.status,
    b.priority,
    u.username
FROM
    Bugs AS b
JOIN
    Users AS u ON b.assigned_to = u.username
WHERE
    u.username = 'john.doe' AND b.priority = 'High';

SELECT
    bug_id,
    title,
    status
FROM
    Bugs
WHERE
    status IN ('Open', 'Reopened');

SELECT
    b.status,
    COUNT(b.bug_id) AS bug_count
FROM
    Bugs AS b
GROUP BY
    b.status
ORDER BY
    bug_count DESC;

Queries:

2. List all overdue loans.
3. Record a new book loan.
4. Mark a book as returned, increasing available copies.
5. Count the number of loans per genre.
text_nat:

FROM Books AS B
JOIN Loans AS L ON B.book_id = L.book_id
WHERE L.borrower_id = 1 AND L.return_date IS NULL;

FROM Loans AS L
JOIN Books AS B ON L.book_id = B.book_id

FROM Books AS B
WHERE B.book_id = 101 AND B.available_copies > 0;

Queries:
1. Find all posts made by a specific user.
2. List all posts within a particular thread.
3. Create a new post in a thread.
4. Update the content of an existing post.
5. Count the number of posts per thread.
text_nat:
SELECT P.post_id, P.content, P.post_date
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Users AS U ON P.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username = 'specific_user_name';

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, P.post_date, U.username
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Threads AS T ON P.thread_id = T.thread_id
JOIN Users AS U ON P.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE T.thread_id = 101;

INSERT INTO Posts (thread_id, user_id, content, post_date)
VALUES (101, 1, 'This is a new post content.', NOW());

UPDATE Posts
SET content = 'Updated content for this post.'
WHERE post_id = 501;

FROM Threads AS T
JOIN Posts AS P ON T.thread_id = P.thread_id
GROUP BY T.title
ORDER BY post_count DESC;

SELECT U.username, P.post_id, P.content
FROM Users AS U JOIN Posts AS P
ON U.user_id = P.user_id
WHERE U.user_id = 2;

FROM Threads AS T JOIN Posts AS P
ON T.thread_id = P.thread_id
WHERE T.thread_id = 102;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, U.username, T.title
FROM Posts AS P JOIN Users AS U
ON P.user_id = U.user_id
JOIN Threads AS T ON P.thread_id = T.thread_id
WHERE U.username = 'another_user';

SELECT U.username, T.title, T.created_at
FROM Users AS U JOIN Threads AS T
ON U.user_id = T.user_id

ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE T.thread_id = 103;

FROM Posts AS P JOIN Threads AS T
ON P.thread_id = T.thread_id
WHERE P.post_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

SELECT U.username, COUNT(P.post_id) AS total_posts
FROM Users AS U JOIN Posts AS P
ON U.user_id = P.user_id
GROUP BY U.username
HAVING COUNT(P.post_id) > 5;

SELECT T.title, COUNT(DISTINCT P.user_id) AS unique_posters
FROM Threads AS T JOIN Posts AS P
ON T.thread_id = P.thread_id
GROUP BY T.title;

SELECT

WHERE
    PC.category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE name = 'Electronics');

    C.name
FROM

Schema: Students (student_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, major VARCHAR), Courses (course_id INT, title VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, credits INT), Enrollments (enrollment_id INT, student_id INT, course_id INT, enrollment_date DATE, grade VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in.
2. List all students enrolled in a particular course.
3. Enroll a student in a new course.
4. Update a student's grade for a course.
5. Count the total credits a student is enrolled in.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Students (student_id, first_name, last_name, major) VALUES
(1, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'Computer Science'),
(2, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'Mathematics');

INSERT INTO Courses (course_id, title, department, credits) VALUES
(101, 'Introduction to SQL', 'Computer Science', 3),
(102, 'Calculus I', 'Mathematics', 4),
(103, 'Data Structures', 'Computer Science', 3);

INSERT INTO Enrollments (enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade) VALUES
(1, 1, 101, '2023-09-01', 'A'),
(2, 1, 103, '2023-09-01', 'B'),
(3, 2, 102, '2023-09-05', 'A');

-- 1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in (e.g., student_id = 1)
SELECT C.title, C.department
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E
ON C.course_id = E.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. List all students enrolled in a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101)
SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E
ON S.student_id = E.student_id
WHERE E.course_id = 101;

-- Another way to get all courses for a specific student, using a different join
SELECT C.title
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE S.first_name = 'Alice';

-- 3. Enroll a student in a new course (e.g., student_id = 2, course_id = 101)
INSERT INTO Enrollments (enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade)
VALUES (4, 2, 101, '2023-10-15', NULL);

-- 4. Update a student's grade for a course (e.g., student_id = 2, course_id = 101, grade = 'B+')
UPDATE Enrollments
SET grade = 'B+'
WHERE student_id = 2 AND course_id = 101;

-- 5. Count the total credits a student is enrolled in (e.g., student_id = 1)
SELECT SUM(C.credits) AS total_credits
FROM Enrollments AS E
JOIN Courses AS C
ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1;

-- Another join example: students with their major and all courses they are enrolled in
SELECT S.first_name, S.major, C.title
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id;

-- Yet another join: courses and the departments of students enrolled in them
SELECT C.title, S.major
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
JOIN Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id;

-- All enrollments with student names and course titles
SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name, C.title, E.enrollment_date
FROM Enrollments AS E
JOIN Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id;

-- All courses with their respective departments and credits, joined with enrollments
SELECT C.title, C.department, C.credits, E.enrollment_date
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id;

-- Students and their enrollments
SELECT S.first_name, E.enrollment_date
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id;

-- Enrollments and the courses involved
SELECT E.enrollment_id, C.title
FROM Enrollments AS E
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id;

-- All students and their majors
SELECT S.first_name, S.major
FROM Students AS S
LEFT JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id;

-- All courses and students enrolled
SELECT C.title, S.first_name
FROM Courses AS C
LEFT JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
LEFT JOIN Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id;

-- Courses with their departments
SELECT C.title, C.department
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Courses AS C2 ON C.department = C2.department;

FROM Actors AS A
JOIN MovieActors AS MA
  ON A.actor_id = MA.actor_id
JOIN Movies AS M
  ON MA.movie_id = M.movie_id
WHERE M.title = 'Inception';

GROUP BY genre;

FROM Movies AS M
JOIN MovieActors AS MA
  ON M.movie_id = MA.movie_id
JOIN Actors AS A
  ON MA.actor_id = A.actor_id

Schema: Jobs (job_id INT, title VARCHAR, company VARCHAR, location VARCHAR, post_date DATE), Applicants (applicant_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Applications (application_id INT, job_id INT, applicant_id INT, application_date DATE, status VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all applications for a specific job.
2. List all jobs applied to by a particular applicant.
3. Submit a new job application.
4. Update an application's status.
5. Count the number of applications per job.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Jobs (job_id, title, company, location, post_date) VALUES
(1, 'Software Engineer', 'TechCorp', 'New York', '2023-01-15'),
(2, 'Data Analyst', 'DataCo', 'San Francisco', '2023-02-01'),
(3, 'Project Manager', 'BuildIt', 'Chicago', '2023-03-10');

INSERT INTO Applicants (applicant_id, first_name, last_name, email) VALUES
(101, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'alice.s@example.com'),
(102, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'bob.j@example.com');

INSERT INTO Applications (application_id, job_id, applicant_id, application_date, status) VALUES
(1001, 1, 101, '2023-01-20', 'Pending'),
(1002, 2, 101, '2023-02-05', 'Approved'),
(1003, 1, 102, '2023-01-22', 'Rejected');

-- 1. Find all applications for a specific job (job_id = 1)
SELECT
    A.application_id,
    A.application_date,
    A.status,
    Ap.first_name,
    Ap.last_name
FROM
    Applications AS A
JOIN
    Applicants AS Ap ON A.applicant_id = Ap.applicant_id
WHERE
    A.job_id = 1;

-- 2. List all jobs applied to by a particular applicant (applicant_id = 101)
SELECT
    J.title,
    J.company,
    A.application_date,
    A.status
FROM
    Applications AS A
JOIN
    Jobs AS J ON A.job_id = J.job_id
WHERE
    A.applicant_id = 101;

-- 3. Submit a new job application
INSERT INTO Applications (application_id, job_id, applicant_id, application_date, status) VALUES
(1004, 3, 101, '2023-03-15', 'Pending');

-- 4. Update an application's status (application_id = 1001 to 'Reviewed')
UPDATE
    Applications
SET
    status = 'Reviewed'
WHERE
    application_id = 1001;

-- 5. Count the number of applications per job
SELECT
    J.title,
    COUNT(A.application_id) AS total_applications
FROM
    Jobs AS J
JOIN
    Applications AS A ON J.job_id = A.job_id
GROUP BY
    J.title;

-- Additional queries with exactly one join

Schema: Items (item_id INT, name VARCHAR, weight DECIMAL, dimensions VARCHAR), Locations (location_id INT, warehouse_name VARCHAR, aisle VARCHAR, rack VARCHAR), ItemLocations (item_id INT, location_id INT, quantity INT, last_moved DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse.
2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
3. Add new stock of an item to a location.
4. Move an item from one location to another.
5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
text_nat:
SELECT
    I.name,
    IL.quantity
FROM
    Items I
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
JOIN
    Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE
    L.warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND L.aisle = 'A1';

SELECT
    L.warehouse_name,
    L.aisle,
    L.rack,
    IL.quantity
FROM
    Locations L
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id
JOIN
    Items I ON IL.item_id = I.item_id
WHERE
    I.name = 'Laptop';

INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved)
SELECT
    (SELECT item_id FROM Items WHERE name = 'Keyboard'),
    (SELECT location_id FROM Locations WHERE warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND aisle = 'A2' AND rack = 'R1'),
    50,
    NOW()
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity, last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved;

UPDATE ItemLocations
SET
    location_id = (SELECT location_id FROM Locations WHERE warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND aisle = 'A3' AND rack = 'R2'),
    last_moved = NOW()
WHERE
    item_id = (SELECT item_id FROM Items WHERE name = 'Mouse')
    AND location_id = (SELECT location_id FROM Locations WHERE warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND aisle = 'A1' AND rack = 'R1');

FROM
    Items I
JOIN

GROUP BY

ORDER BY total_feedback DESC;

SELECT F.feedback_id, C.name AS customer_name
FROM Feedback AS F, Customers AS C
WHERE F.customer_id = C.customer_id;

SELECT F.feedback_id, P.name AS product_name
FROM Feedback AS F, Products AS P
WHERE F.product_id = P.product_id;

SELECT C.customer_id, C.name, COUNT(F.feedback_id) AS feedback_count
FROM Customers AS C
LEFT JOIN Feedback AS F ON C.customer_id = F.customer_id
GROUP BY C.customer_id, C.name
ORDER BY feedback_count DESC;

SELECT F.feedback_id, F.rating, F.comments, C.name AS customer_name, P.name AS product_name
FROM Feedback AS F, Customers AS C, Products AS P
WHERE F.customer_id = C.customer_id AND F.product_id = P.product_id
AND F.feedback_date >= '2023-01-01' AND F.rating >= 4;

SELECT P.name AS product_name, P.description
FROM Products AS P
LEFT JOIN Feedback AS F ON P.product_id = F.product_id
WHERE F.feedback_id IS NULL;

SELECT C.name, C.email, F.feedback_date
FROM Customers AS C, Feedback AS F
WHERE C.customer_id = F.customer_id
ORDER BY F.feedback_date DESC;

SELECT P.name, AVG(F.rating) AS avg_rating
FROM Products AS P, Feedback AS F
WHERE P.product_id = F.product_id
GROUP BY P.name;

Queries:

3. Record a new transaction.
4. Update a transaction's status.
5. Calculate the total amount of transactions per currency.

FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username = 'specific_user_name' AND T.status = 'completed';

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.amount, T.currency, T.transaction_date, U.username
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE T.status = 'failed';

INSERT INTO Transactions (user_id, amount, currency, transaction_date, status)
VALUES (1, 50.00, 'USD', NOW(), 'pending');

SET status = 'completed'
WHERE transaction_id = 123;

SELECT currency, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
FROM Transactions
GROUP BY currency;

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.amount
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.email = 'user@example.com';

SELECT U.username, T.transaction_id
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
WHERE T.amount > 100;

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.currency
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE T.transaction_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

SELECT U.username, T.status
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
WHERE T.status = 'pending';

SELECT T.amount, U.email
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
ORDER BY T.amount DESC;

SELECT U.username, U.email
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
GROUP BY U.user_id
HAVING COUNT(T.transaction_id) > 5;

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.transaction_date
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username LIKE 'A%';

SELECT U.username, T.currency
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
WHERE T.currency = 'EUR';

SELECT T.status, COUNT(T.transaction_id) AS transaction_count
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
GROUP BY T.status;

text_nat:
SELECT pet_id, name, species, breed, age

JOIN Adoptions AS a ON ad.adopter_id = a.adopter_id;

Schema: Patients (patient_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, date_of_birth DATE, gender VARCHAR), Doctors (doctor_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, specialty VARCHAR), Visits (visit_id INT, patient_id INT, doctor_id INT, visit_date DATETIME, diagnosis TEXT).
Queries:
1. Find all visits for a specific patient.
2. List all patients seen by a particular doctor.
3. Record a new patient visit.
4. Update a patient's diagnosis for a visit.
5. Count the number of visits per doctor's specialty.
text_nat:
SELECT
    P.first_name, P.last_name, V.visit_date, V.diagnosis
FROM
    Patients AS P
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON P.patient_id = V.patient_id
WHERE
    P.patient_id = 1;

SELECT
    P.first_name, P.last_name, P.date_of_birth
FROM
    Patients AS P
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON P.patient_id = V.patient_id
WHERE
    V.doctor_id = 101;

VALUES (2, 102, '2023-11-15 10:00:00', 'Common cold');

UPDATE Visits
SET diagnosis = 'Influenza'
WHERE visit_id = 5;

SELECT
    D.specialty, COUNT(V.visit_id) AS total_visits
FROM
    Doctors AS D
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON D.doctor_id = V.doctor_id
GROUP BY
    D.specialty;

SELECT
    P.first_name, P.last_name, V.visit_date
FROM
    Patients AS P
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON P.patient_id = V.patient_id;

SELECT
    D.first_name, D.last_name, D.specialty, V.visit_date
FROM
    Doctors AS D
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON D.doctor_id = V.doctor_id;

SELECT
    P.first_name, P.last_name, D.specialty
FROM
    Patients AS P
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON P.patient_id = V.patient_id
JOIN
    Doctors AS D ON V.doctor_id = D.doctor_id
WHERE
    P.patient_id = 3;

SELECT
    D.first_name AS doctor_first_name, D.last_name AS doctor_last_name,
    P.first_name AS patient_first_name, P.last_name AS patient_last_name,
    V.visit_date, V.diagnosis
FROM
    Doctors AS D
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON D.doctor_id = V.doctor_id
JOIN
    Patients AS P ON V.patient_id = P.patient_id
WHERE
    D.specialty = 'Pediatrics';

SELECT
    P.first_name, P.last_name
FROM
    Patients AS P
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON P.patient_id = V.patient_id
WHERE
    V.diagnosis LIKE '%Flu%';

SELECT
    D.first_name, D.last_name, COUNT(V.visit_id) AS num_visits
FROM
    Doctors AS D
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON D.doctor_id = V.doctor_id
GROUP BY
    D.doctor_id;

SELECT
    P.first_name, P.last_name
FROM
    Patients AS P
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON P.patient_id = V.patient_id
WHERE
    V.visit_date > '2023-01-01';

SELECT
    D.specialty, P.gender, COUNT(V.visit_id) AS visits_count

    Doctors AS D
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON D.doctor_id = V.doctor_id
JOIN
    Patients AS P ON V.patient_id = P.patient_id
GROUP BY
    D.specialty, P.gender;

SELECT
    P.first_name, P.last_name, D.specialty, V.visit_date, V.diagnosis
FROM
    Patients AS P
JOIN
    Visits AS V ON P.patient_id = V.patient_id
JOIN
    Doctors AS D ON V.doctor_id = D.doctor_id
ORDER BY
    V.visit_date DESC;

    Patients AS P, Visits AS V, Doctors AS D

FROM Responses AS R
JOIN Questions AS Q

Schema: Artists (artist_id INT, name VARCHAR, genre VARCHAR), Albums (album_id INT, artist_id INT, title VARCHAR, release_year INT), Tracks (track_id INT, album_id INT, title VARCHAR, duration_seconds INT).
Queries:

2. List all tracks on a particular album.
3. Add a new album.
4. Update the release year of an album.
5. Count the total duration of tracks per album.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Artists (
    artist_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Albums (
    album_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    artist_id INT,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    release_year INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (artist_id) REFERENCES Artists(artist_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Tracks (
    track_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    album_id INT,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    duration_seconds INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (album_id) REFERENCES Albums(album_id)
);

-- Query 1: Find all albums by a specific artist ('Artist A')

    A.title AS album_title,
    A.release_year
FROM
    Albums AS A
JOIN
    Artists AS B ON A.artist_id = B.artist_id
WHERE
    B.name = 'Artist A';

-- Query 2: List all tracks on a particular album ('Album X')

    T.title AS track_title,
    T.duration_seconds
FROM
    Tracks AS T
JOIN

    AL.title = 'Album X';

Schema: Teams (team_id INT, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR), Matches (match_id INT, home_team_id INT, away_team_id INT, match_date DATETIME, home_score INT, away_score INT), Players (player_id INT, team_id INT, name VARCHAR, position VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all matches played by a specific team.
2. List all players on a particular team.
3. Record a new match score.
4. Update a player's position.
5. Calculate the total wins for each team.

INSERT INTO Teams (team_id, name, city) VALUES (1, 'Real Madrid', 'Madrid');

-- 1. Find all matches played by a specific team (e.g., 'Real Madrid')
SELECT m.*
FROM Matches m
JOIN Teams t ON m.home_team_id = t.team_id
WHERE t.name = 'Real Madrid'
UNION ALL
SELECT m.*
FROM Matches m
JOIN Teams t ON m.away_team_id = t.team_id
WHERE t.name = 'Real Madrid';

-- 2. List all players on a particular team (e.g., 'Barcelona')
SELECT p.name, p.position
FROM Players p
JOIN Teams t ON p.team_id = t.team_id
WHERE t.name = 'Barcelona';

-- 3. Record a new match score (assuming match_id 3 already exists with null scores)
UPDATE Matches
SET home_score = 3, away_score = 0
WHERE match_id = 1;

-- 4. Update a player's position (e.g., player_id 1 to 'Striker')
UPDATE Players
SET position = 'Striker'
WHERE player_id = 1;

-- 5. Calculate the total wins for each team
SELECT t.name, COUNT(t.team_id) AS total_wins
FROM Teams t
JOIN Matches m ON t.team_id = m.home_team_id AND m.home_score > m.away_score
GROUP BY t.name
UNION ALL
SELECT t.name, COUNT(t.team_id) AS total_wins
FROM Teams t
JOIN Matches m ON t.team_id = m.away_team_id AND m.away_score > m.home_score
GROUP BY t.name;

FROM Players P
JOIN Teams T ON P.team_id = T.team_id;

JOIN Teams T ON M.away_team_id = T.team_id;

WHERE T.city = 'Madrid';

FROM Teams T
JOIN Matches M ON T.team_id = M.home_team_id
GROUP BY T.name;

SELECT T.name, COUNT(M.match_id) AS away_matches
FROM Teams T
JOIN Matches M ON T.team_id = M.away_team_id
GROUP BY T.name;

SELECT P.name, P.position
FROM Players P
JOIN Teams T ON P.team_id = T.team_id
WHERE T.name = 'Real Madrid';

SELECT M.match_id, M.match_date
FROM Matches M
JOIN Teams T ON M.home_team_id = T.team_id
WHERE T.name = 'Barcelona';

Queries:

2. List all students enrolled in a particular course.

4. Update a student's completion status for a course.
5. Count the number of enrolled students per course.

Schema: Products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, supplier_id INT), Suppliers (supplier_id INT, name VARCHAR, contact_email VARCHAR), Stock (product_id INT, quantity INT, last_updated DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all products supplied by a specific supplier.
2. List all products with stock quantity below 10.
3. Add a new product to stock.
4. Update the price of a product.
5. Calculate the total value of stock for each category.
text_nat:
SELECT P.name, P.category, P.price
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Suppliers AS S
ON P.supplier_id = S.supplier_id
WHERE S.name = 'Supplier A';

SELECT P.name, S.quantity
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Stock AS S
ON P.product_id = S.product_id
WHERE S.quantity < 10;

SET price = 54.99
WHERE product_id = 101;

SELECT P.category, SUM(P.price * ST.quantity) AS total_value
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Stock AS ST
ON P.product_id = ST.product_id
GROUP BY P.category;

SELECT P.name, P.category, S.name AS supplier_name
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Suppliers AS S
ON P.supplier_id = S.supplier_id;

SELECT P.name, ST.quantity

JOIN Stock AS ST
ON P.product_id = ST.product_id;

FROM Suppliers AS S
JOIN Products AS P
ON S.supplier_id = P.supplier_id;

SELECT P.name, ST.last_updated

JOIN Stock AS ST
ON P.product_id = ST.product_id;

SELECT S.name, S.contact_email
FROM Suppliers AS S
JOIN Products AS P

WHERE P.category = 'Electronics';

SELECT P.name, P.price
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Stock AS ST

JOIN Stock AS S

SELECT S.name, S.contact_email

JOIN Products AS P
ON S.supplier_id = P.supplier_id;
