Schema: Projects (project_id INT, name VARCHAR, manager_id INT, start_date DATE, end_date DATE), Employees (employee_id INT, name VARCHAR, position VARCHAR), ProjectAssignments (project_id INT, employee_id INT, role VARCHAR, start_date DATE, end_date DATE).
Queries:
1. Find all employees assigned to a specific project.
2. List all projects managed by a particular employee.
3. Assign an employee to a project.
4. Update an employee's role on a project.
5. Count the number of employees per project.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all employees assigned to a specific project.
SELECT E.name AS employee_name, PA.role
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
WHERE PA.project_id = 1;

-- 2. List all projects managed by a particular employee.
SELECT P.name AS project_name, P.start_date, P.end_date
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN Employees AS E ON P.manager_id = E.employee_id
WHERE E.employee_id = 2;

-- 3. Assign an employee to a project (example: employee 3 to project 2, role 'Developer').
INSERT INTO ProjectAssignments (project_id, employee_id, role, start_date, end_date)
VALUES (2, 3, 'Developer', '2023-01-15', '2023-06-15');

-- 4. Update an employee's role on a project (example: employee 3 on project 2 to 'Lead Developer').
UPDATE ProjectAssignments
SET role = 'Lead Developer'
WHERE project_id = 2 AND employee_id = 3;

-- 5. Count the number of employees per project.
SELECT P.name AS project_name, COUNT(PA.employee_id) AS number_of_employees
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON P.project_id = PA.project_id
GROUP BY P.name;

SELECT P.name AS project_name, E.name AS manager_name
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN Employees AS E ON P.manager_id = E.employee_id;

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, PA.role, P.name AS project_name
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
JOIN Projects AS P ON PA.project_id = P.project_id
WHERE E.employee_id = 1;

SELECT P.name AS project_name, P.start_date, P.end_date, E.name AS manager_name
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN Employees AS E ON P.manager_id = E.employee_id
WHERE P.start_date < '2023-03-01';

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, PA.role
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
WHERE PA.end_date > '2023-04-01';

SELECT P.name AS project_name, PA.role, E.name AS employee_name
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON P.project_id = PA.project_id
JOIN Employees AS E ON PA.employee_id = E.employee_id
WHERE PA.role = 'Developer';

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, P.name AS project_name
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
JOIN Projects AS P ON PA.project_id = P.project_id
WHERE P.project_id = 1;

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, E.position
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
WHERE PA.role = 'Tester';

SELECT P.name AS project_name, E.name AS employee_name
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON P.project_id = PA.project_id
JOIN Employees AS E ON PA.employee_id = E.employee_id
WHERE P.manager_id = 2;

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, registration_date DATETIME, last_login DATETIME), Pages (page_id INT, url VARCHAR, title VARCHAR), PageViews (view_id INT, user_id INT, page_id INT, view_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all pages viewed by a specific user.
2. List the top 5 most viewed pages.
3. Record a new page view.
4. Update a user's last login date.
5. Count the total page views for each user.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Find all pages viewed by a specific user (e.g., user_id = 1)
SELECT DISTINCT P.title, P.url
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE PV.user_id = 1;

-- Query 2: List the top 5 most viewed pages
SELECT P.title, COUNT(PV.page_id) AS view_count
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY P.title
ORDER BY view_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- Query 3: Record a new page view
-- (Assuming user_id = 1, page_id = 2, view_date = '2023-10-27 10:30:00')
INSERT INTO PageViews (user_id, page_id, view_date)
VALUES (1, 2, '2023-10-27 10:30:00');

-- Query 4: Update a user's last login date (e.g., user_id = 1)
UPDATE Users
SET last_login = '2023-10-27 10:35:00'
WHERE user_id = 1;

-- Query 5: Count the total page views for each user
SELECT U.username, COUNT(PV.view_id) AS total_views
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY U.username
ORDER BY total_views DESC;

-- Additional queries with single JOINs:

-- Find all users who viewed a specific page (e.g., page_id = 3)
SELECT U.username
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
WHERE PV.page_id = 3;

-- Get page details for a specific view_id (e.g., view_id = 5)
SELECT P.title, P.url
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE PV.view_id = 5;

-- Get user details for a specific view_id (e.g., view_id = 5)
SELECT U.username, U.registration_date
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
WHERE PV.view_id = 5;

-- List all pages and their titles
SELECT P.page_id, P.title
FROM Pages AS P;

-- List users who have logged in after their registration date
SELECT U.username
FROM Users AS U
WHERE U.last_login > U.registration_date;

-- Count views per page, ordered by page_id
SELECT P.title, COUNT(PV.page_id)
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY P.page_id
ORDER BY P.page_id;

-- Get the latest view date for each user
SELECT U.username, MAX(PV.view_date) AS latest_view
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

-- Find pages viewed on a specific date (e.g., '2023-10-27')
SELECT DISTINCT P.title
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE DATE(PV.view_date) = '2023-10-27';

Queries:
1. Find all commits made by a specific user in a repository.
2. List all repositories owned by a particular user.
3. Record a new commit to a repository.
4. Update a repository's name.
5. Count the number of commits per repository.
text_nat:
SELECT
  C.commit_id,
  C.commit_message,
  C.commit_date
FROM Commits AS C
JOIN Users AS U

Schema: Pilots (pilot_id INT, name VARCHAR, license_number VARCHAR), Aircraft (aircraft_id INT, type VARCHAR, registration VARCHAR), Flights (flight_id INT, pilot_id INT, aircraft_id INT, flight_date DATETIME, duration_hours DECIMAL, origin VARCHAR, destination VARCHAR).

Schema: Routes (route_id INT, route_number VARCHAR, description TEXT), Stops (stop_id INT, name VARCHAR, latitude DECIMAL, longitude DECIMAL), RouteStops (route_id INT, stop_id INT, stop_order INT).
Queries:
1. Find all stops for a specific route.
2. List all routes that pass through a particular stop.
3. Add a new stop to a route.
4. Update a stop's latitude and longitude.
5. Count the number of stops per route.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all stops for a specific route (e.g., route_id = 1)
SELECT S.name, S.latitude, S.longitude
FROM Stops AS S
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON S.stop_id = RS.stop_id
WHERE RS.route_id = 1
ORDER BY RS.stop_order;

-- 2. List all routes that pass through a particular stop (e.g., stop_id = 101)
SELECT R.route_number, R.description
FROM Routes AS R
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
WHERE RS.stop_id = 101;

-- Add a new stop to a route (e.g., route_id = 2, stop_id = 105, at order 3)
INSERT INTO RouteStops (route_id, stop_id, stop_order)
VALUES (2, 105, 3);

-- Update a stop's latitude and longitude (e.g., stop_id = 102)
UPDATE Stops
SET latitude = 34.0522, longitude = -118.2437
WHERE stop_id = 102;

-- 5. Count the number of stops per route
SELECT R.route_number, COUNT(RS.stop_id) AS num_stops
FROM Routes AS R
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
GROUP BY R.route_number
ORDER BY num_stops DESC;

-- Example query 1: All stops on a route, including route description
SELECT S.name, S.latitude, S.longitude, R.description
FROM Stops AS S
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON S.stop_id = RS.stop_id
JOIN Routes AS R ON RS.route_id = R.route_id
WHERE R.route_number = 'A101'
ORDER BY RS.stop_order;

-- Example query 2: Routes and their first stop
SELECT R.route_number, R.description, S.name AS first_stop_name
FROM Routes AS R
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
JOIN Stops AS S ON RS.stop_id = S.stop_id
WHERE RS.stop_order = 1;

-- Example query 3: Stops that are part of more than one route
SELECT S.name, COUNT(RS.route_id) AS num_routes
FROM Stops AS S
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON S.stop_id = RS.stop_id
GROUP BY S.name
HAVING COUNT(RS.route_id) > 1;

-- Example query 4: Routes with no stops
SELECT R.route_number
FROM Routes AS R
LEFT JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
WHERE RS.stop_id IS NULL;

-- Example single-join query: Get route number for each RouteStop entry
SELECT RS.route_id, R.route_number
FROM RouteStops AS RS
JOIN Routes AS R ON RS.route_id = R.route_id;

-- Another single-join query: Get stop name for each RouteStop entry
SELECT RS.stop_id, S.name
FROM RouteStops AS RS
JOIN Stops AS S ON RS.stop_id = S.stop_id;

-- Single-join query: Find stops by name (e.g., 'Central Station')
SELECT S.stop_id, S.latitude, S.longitude
FROM Stops AS S
WHERE S.name = 'Central Station';

-- Single-join query: All routes and their route number
SELECT route_id, route_number
FROM Routes;

-- Single-join query: All stops and their details
SELECT stop_id, name, latitude, longitude
FROM Stops;

-- Single-join query: All route-stop relationships
SELECT route_id, stop_id, stop_order
FROM RouteStops;

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Conversations (conversation_id INT, user1_id INT, user2_id INT, created_at DATETIME), Messages (message_id INT, conversation_id INT, sender_id INT, content TEXT, sent_at DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all messages in a specific conversation.
2. List all conversations involving a particular user.
3. Send a new message in a conversation.
4. Update a user's email.
5. Count the number of messages sent by each user.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Messages
JOIN Conversations ON Messages.conversation_id = Conversations.conversation_id
WHERE Messages.conversation_id = 1;

SELECT C.conversation_id, U1.username AS user1_username, U2.username AS user2_username
FROM Conversations AS C
JOIN Users AS U1 ON C.user1_id = U1.user_id
JOIN Users AS U2 ON C.user2_id = U2.user_id
WHERE C.user1_id = 1 OR C.user2_id = 1;

INSERT INTO Messages (conversation_id, sender_id, content, sent_at)
VALUES (1, 2, 'Hello there!', NOW());

UPDATE Users
SET email = 'new_email@example.com'
WHERE user_id = 1;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(M.message_id) AS message_count
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Messages AS M ON U.user_id = M.sender_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT C.conversation_id, COUNT(M.message_id) AS total_messages
FROM Conversations AS C
JOIN Messages AS M ON C.conversation_id = M.conversation_id
GROUP BY C.conversation_id;

SELECT U.username, M.content
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Messages AS M ON U.user_id = M.sender_id
WHERE M.conversation_id = 1;

SELECT C.conversation_id, U.username
FROM Conversations AS C
JOIN Users AS U ON C.user1_id = U.user_id;

SELECT M.content, C.created_at
FROM Messages AS M
JOIN Conversations AS C ON M.conversation_id = C.conversation_id;

SELECT U.username, U.email
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Conversations AS C ON U.user_id = C.user1_id
WHERE C.conversation_id = 2;

SELECT M.message_id, M.content, U.username AS sender_username
FROM Messages AS M
JOIN Users AS U ON M.sender_id = U.user_id
WHERE M.conversation_id = 3;

SELECT U.username, U.email, C.created_at
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Conversations AS C ON U.user1_id = C.user_id
OR U.user2_id = C.user_id
WHERE U.user_id = 1;

Queries:
1. Find all transactions for a specific account.
2. List all accounts belonging to a particular user.
3. Record a new transaction for an account.
4. Update an account's balance (e.g., after a transaction).
5. Calculate the total spending by transaction type for a user.
text_nat:
SELECT transaction_id, type, amount, transaction_date, description
FROM Transactions
WHERE account_id = 101;

SELECT A.account_id, A.account_name, A.balance
FROM Accounts A
JOIN Users U ON A.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.user_id = 201;

SET balance = balance + 500.00
WHERE account_id = 101;

SELECT T.type, SUM(T.amount) AS total_spending
FROM Transactions T
JOIN Accounts A ON T.account_id = A.account_id
JOIN Users U ON A.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.user_id = 201 AND T.type = 'withdrawal'
GROUP BY T.type;

text_es:
Schema: 
`Books` (book_id PK, title, author_id, genre, publication_date, status)
`Authors` (author_id PK, first_name, last_name, email)
`Editors` (editor_id PK, first_name, last_name, specialty)

Queries:
1. Get all books published by a specific author, ordered by publication date.
2. Count the number of books in each genre.
3. Find books currently in 'Editing' status and their authors.
4. Insert a new book and its author.
5. Update the status of a book from 'Draft' to 'Submitted for Review'.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Get all books published by a specific author, ordered by publication date.
SELECT
    B.title,
    B.publication_date
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN
    Authors AS A
ON
    B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    A.first_name = 'Jane' AND A.last_name = 'Doe'
ORDER BY
    B.publication_date;

-- Query 2: Count the number of books in each genre.
SELECT
    genre,
    COUNT(book_id) AS number_of_books
FROM
    Books
GROUP BY
    genre;

-- Query 3: Find books currently in 'Editing' status and their authors.
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.status = 'Editing';

-- Query 4: Insert a new book and its author.
INSERT INTO Authors (author_id, first_name, last_name, email)
VALUES (4, 'New', 'Author', 'new.author@example.com');

INSERT INTO Books (book_id, title, author_id, genre, publication_date, status)
VALUES (6, 'The New Adventure', 4, 'Adventure', '2023-10-26', 'Draft');

-- Query 5: Update the status of a book from 'Draft' to 'Submitted for Review'.
UPDATE
    Books
SET
    status = 'Submitted for Review'
WHERE
    book_id = 1 AND status = 'Draft';

-- Additional queries with single JOINs

-- Get all books by authors whose last name starts with 'S'
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    A.last_name LIKE 'S%';

-- Get all authors and the titles of their books
SELECT
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name,
    B.title
FROM
    Authors AS A
JOIN Books AS B
ON A.author_id = B.author_id;

-- Find books published after 2020 and their author's email
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.email
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.publication_date > '2020-01-01';

-- List all authors and books, even if an author has no books (LEFT JOIN)
SELECT
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name,
    B.title
FROM
    Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Books AS B
ON A.author_id = B.author_id;

-- Find books with 'Fantasy' genre and their authors' full names
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.first_name || ' ' || A.last_name AS author_full_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.genre = 'Fantasy';

-- Get the title of books and the specialty of editors (no direct link, so this is just an example of a join with a condition)
-- This specific query would only make sense if there was a link between Books and Editors, but for the sake of the exercise...
SELECT
    B.title,
    E.specialty
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Editors AS E
ON B.book_id = E.editor_id  -- Assuming a hypothetical link or for illustration
WHERE
    E.specialty = 'Fiction';

SELECT DISTINCT
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name
FROM
    Authors AS A
JOIN Books AS B
ON A.author_id = B.author_id
WHERE
    B.genre = 'Mystery';

SELECT
    B.title,
    A.last_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.status = 'Published';

Schema: 
`Courses` (course_id PK, course_name, instructor_id, credits)
`Students` (student_id PK, first_name, last_name, email)
`Enrollments` (enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, grade)

Queries:
1. List all courses a specific student is enrolled in, including their grades.
2. Find all students enrolled in a particular course.
3. Count the number of students enrolled in each course.
4. Enroll a student in a new course.
5. Update the grade for a specific student in a specific course.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all courses a specific student is enrolled in, including their grades.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    E.grade
FROM
    Enrollments AS E
JOIN
    Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE
    E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all students enrolled in a particular course.
SELECT
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name
FROM
    Enrollments AS E
JOIN
    Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id
WHERE
    E.course_id = 101;

-- 3. Count the number of students enrolled in each course.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    COUNT(E.student_id) AS student_count
FROM
    Courses AS C
LEFT JOIN
    Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.course_name;

-- 4. Enroll a student in a new course.
INSERT INTO Enrollments (student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade)
SELECT
    S.student_id,
    C.course_id,
    CURRENT_DATE,
    NULL
FROM
    Students AS S
JOIN
    Courses AS C ON C.course_id = 103 -- Assuming course_id 103 for the new course
WHERE
    S.student_id = 2; -- Assuming student_id 2 for the student to enroll

-- 5. Update the grade for a specific student in a specific course.
UPDATE Enrollments
SET grade = 'A'
FROM
    Students AS S
JOIN
    Courses AS C ON Enrollments.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE
    Enrollments.student_id = S.student_id
    AND S.student_id = 1
    AND Enrollments.course_id = 101;
text_alt:
-- 1. List all courses a specific student is enrolled in, including their grades.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    E.grade
FROM
    Enrollments AS E,
    Courses AS C
WHERE
    E.course_id = C.course_id
    AND E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all students enrolled in a particular course.
SELECT
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name
FROM
    Enrollments AS E,
    Students AS S
WHERE
    E.student_id = S.student_id
    AND E.course_id = 101;

-- 3. Count the number of students enrolled in each course.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    COUNT(E.student_id) AS student_count
FROM
    Courses AS C
LEFT JOIN
    Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.course_name;

-- 4. Enroll a student in a new course.
INSERT INTO Enrollments (student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade)
SELECT
    S.student_id,
    C.course_id,
    CURRENT_DATE,
    NULL
FROM
    Students AS S,
    Courses AS C
WHERE
    C.course_id = 103 -- Assuming course_id 103 for the new course
    AND S.student_id = 2; -- Assuming student_id 2 for the student to enroll

-- 5. Update the grade for a specific student in a specific course.
UPDATE Enrollments
SET grade = 'A'
FROM
    Students AS S,
    Courses AS C
WHERE
    Enrollments.course_id = C.course_id
    AND Enrollments.student_id = S.student_id
    AND S.student_id = 1
    AND Enrollments.course_id = 101;

FROM Artists AS A
LEFT JOIN Performances AS P
  ON A.artist_id = P.artist_id

  A.artist_name
ORDER BY

Schema: 
`Employees` (employee_id PK, first_name, last_name, department_id)
`Goals` (goal_id PK, employee_id FK, goal_description, target_date, actual_completion_date, status)

Queries:
1. List all active goals for a specific employee.
2. Find all employees with overdue goals.
3. Count the number of goals by status for each department.
4. Assign a new goal to an employee.
5. Update the status of a goal to 'Completed'.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all active goals for a specific employee.
SELECT
    G.goal_description,
    G.target_date
FROM
    Goals AS G
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON G.employee_id = E.employee_id
WHERE
    E.employee_id = 101 AND G.status = 'In Progress';

-- 2. Find all employees with overdue goals.
SELECT DISTINCT
    E.first_name,
    E.last_name
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    Goals AS G ON E.employee_id = G.employee_id
WHERE
    G.status != 'Completed' AND G.target_date < CURRENT_DATE;

-- 3. Count the number of goals by status for each department.
SELECT
    D.department_name,
    G.status,
    COUNT(G.goal_id) AS goal_count
FROM
    Goals AS G
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON G.employee_id = E.employee_id
JOIN
    Departments AS D ON E.department_id = D.department_id
GROUP BY
    D.department_name, G.status
ORDER BY
    D.department_name, G.status;

-- 4. Assign a new goal to an employee.
INSERT INTO Goals (employee_id, goal_description, target_date, status)
SELECT
    E.employee_id,
    'Improve SQL skills',
    '2024-12-31',
    'In Progress'
FROM
    Employees AS E
WHERE
    E.employee_id = 102;

-- 5. Update the status of a goal to 'Completed'.
UPDATE Goals
SET
    status = 'Completed',
    actual_completion_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE
    goal_id = 205;

Schema: 
`Transactions` (transaction_id PK, customer_id, transaction_date, total_amount)
`TransactionItems` (item_id PK, transaction_id FK, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
`Products` (product_id PK, product_name, category)

Queries:
1. Get all items for a specific transaction, including product names.
2. Calculate the total sales for each product category within a date range.
3. Find all transactions made by a specific customer.
4. Insert a new transaction with multiple items.
5. Update the total amount of a transaction.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Get all items for a specific transaction, including product names.
SELECT
    ti.item_id,
    ti.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    ti.quantity,
    ti.unit_price
FROM
    TransactionItems ti
JOIN
    Products p ON ti.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
    ti.transaction_id = 101;

-- Query 2: Calculate the total sales for each product category within a date range.
SELECT
    p.category,
    SUM(ti.quantity * ti.unit_price) AS total_sales
FROM
    Transactions t
JOIN
    TransactionItems ti ON t.transaction_id = ti.transaction_id
JOIN
    Products p ON ti.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
    t.transaction_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31'
GROUP BY
    p.category;

-- Query 3: Find all transactions made by a specific customer.
SELECT
    t.transaction_id,
    t.transaction_date,
    t.total_amount
FROM
    Transactions t
WHERE
    t.customer_id = 5;

-- Query 4: Insert a new transaction with multiple items.
INSERT INTO Transactions (transaction_id, customer_id, transaction_date, total_amount)
VALUES (105, 7, '2023-02-15', 0);

INSERT INTO TransactionItems (item_id, transaction_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
SELECT 201, 105, 301, 2, 10.50
UNION ALL
SELECT 202, 105, 302, 1, 25.00;

-- Query 5: Update the total amount of a transaction.
UPDATE Transactions t
SET total_amount = (
    SELECT SUM(ti.quantity * ti.unit_price)
    FROM TransactionItems ti
    WHERE ti.transaction_id = t.transaction_id
)
WHERE t.transaction_id = 105;

`Fuelings` (fueling_id PK, vehicle_id FK, fueling_date, mileage_at_fueling, fuel_amount_liters, cost)

Queries:

2. Calculate the average fuel cost per liter for each vehicle.
3. Find the total fuel consumed by all vehicles in a given month.
4. Insert a new fueling record for a vehicle.
5. Update the current mileage of a vehicle after fueling.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Fuelings f
JOIN Vehicles v ON f.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
WHERE v.license_plate = 'ABC-123'
ORDER BY f.fueling_date DESC;

SELECT
    v.make,
    v.model,
    AVG(f.cost / f.fuel_amount_liters) AS average_cost_per_liter
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN Fuelings f ON v.vehicle_id = f.vehicle_id
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id, v.make, v.model;

SELECT
    SUM(f.fuel_amount_liters) AS total_fuel_consumed_liters
FROM Fuelings f
WHERE STRFTIME('%Y-%m', f.fueling_date) = '2023-10';

Schema: 
`Rooms` (room_id PK, room_number, floor, capacity, status)
`Patients` (patient_id PK, first_name, last_name, admission_date)
`Admissions` (admission_id PK, patient_id FK, room_id FK, admission_start_date, admission_end_date)

Queries:
1. List all occupied rooms and the patients in them.
2. Find all available rooms on a specific floor.
3. Count the number of occupied rooms by floor.
4. Admit a patient to an available room.
5. Update the status of a room to 'Vacant' after a patient discharge.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all occupied rooms and the patients in them.
SELECT
  R.room_number,
  P.first_name,
  P.last_name
FROM Rooms AS R
JOIN Admissions AS A
  ON R.room_id = A.room_id
JOIN Patients AS P
  ON A.patient_id = P.patient_id
WHERE
  R.status = 'Occupied' AND A.admission_end_date IS NULL;

-- 2. Find all available rooms on a specific floor (e.g., floor 3).
SELECT
  room_number,
  capacity
FROM Rooms
WHERE
  status = 'Available' AND floor = 3;

-- 3. Count the number of occupied rooms by floor.
SELECT
  R.floor,
  COUNT(R.room_id) AS occupied_rooms_count
FROM Rooms AS R
JOIN Admissions AS A
  ON R.room_id = A.room_id
WHERE
  R.status = 'Occupied' AND A.admission_end_date IS NULL
GROUP BY
  R.floor;

-- 4. Admit a patient to an available room (patient_id 101, room_id 201).
INSERT INTO Admissions (patient_id, room_id, admission_start_date, admission_end_date)
VALUES
  (101, 201, '2023-10-26', NULL);

UPDATE Rooms
SET
  status = 'Occupied'
WHERE
  room_id = 201;

-- 5. Update the status of a room to 'Vacant' after a patient discharge (admission_id 301).
UPDATE Admissions
SET
  admission_end_date = '2023-10-27'
WHERE
  admission_id = 301;

UPDATE Rooms
SET
  status = 'Available'
WHERE
  room_id = (SELECT
               room_id
             FROM Admissions
             WHERE
               admission_id = 301);

Queries:
1. List the progress of a specific user in all their enrolled courses.
2. Find all users who have completed a particular course.
3. Calculate the average completed modules for each course.
4. Record a user's progress in a course.
5. Update the 'status' of a user's course progress to 'Completed'.
text_nat:
-- 1. List the progress of a specific user in all their enrolled courses.
SELECT
    u.username,
    c.course_name,
    p.completed_modules,
    p.total_modules,
    p.status
FROM
    Users AS u
JOIN
    Progress AS p ON u.user_id = p.user_id
JOIN
    Courses AS c ON p.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE

    u.email
FROM
    Users AS u
JOIN

WHERE
    p.course_id = 101 AND p.status = 'Completed';

SELECT
    c.course_name,
    AVG(p.completed_modules) AS average_completed_modules
FROM
    Courses AS c
LEFT JOIN
    Progress AS p ON c.course_id = p.course_id
GROUP BY
    c.course_name;

Schema: 
`Teams` (team_id PK, team_name, sport, city)
`Players` (player_id PK, first_name, last_name, position, team_id FK)
`Games` (game_id PK, home_team_id FK, away_team_id FK, game_date, score_home, score_away)

Queries:
1. List all players for a specific team, including their positions.
2. Find all games played by a specific team within a date range.
3. Count the number of players on each team.
4. Add a new player to a team.
5. Update the score for a specific game.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all players for a specific team, including their positions.
SELECT
    p.first_name,
    p.last_name,
    p.position
FROM
    Players AS p
JOIN
    Teams AS t ON p.team_id = t.team_id
WHERE
    t.team_name = 'Lakers';

-- 2. Find all games played by a specific team within a date range.
SELECT
    g.game_date,
    th.team_name AS home_team,
    ta.team_name AS away_team,
    g.score_home,
    g.score_away
FROM
    Games AS g
JOIN
    Teams AS th ON g.home_team_id = th.team_id
JOIN
    Teams AS ta ON g.away_team_id = ta.team_id
WHERE
    (th.team_name = 'Lakers' OR ta.team_name = 'Lakers')
    AND g.game_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-03-31';

-- 3. Count the number of players on each team.
SELECT
    t.team_name,
    COUNT(p.player_id) AS player_count
FROM
    Teams AS t
LEFT JOIN
    Players AS p ON t.team_id = p.team_id
GROUP BY
    t.team_name;

-- 4. Add a new player to a team.
INSERT INTO Players (player_id, first_name, last_name, position, team_id)
SELECT
    101, 'New', 'Player', 'Guard', t.team_id
FROM

text_es:
Schema: 
`Customers` (customer_id PK, first_name, last_name, email, join_date)
`Tiers` (tier_id PK, tier_name, min_points, max_points, benefits)
`LoyaltyPoints` (point_id PK, customer_id FK, points_earned, transaction_date, description)

Queries:
1. Get the current loyalty points for a specific customer.
2. Find all customers in a particular loyalty tier.
3. Calculate the total points earned by each customer.
4. Award loyalty points to a customer for a transaction.
5. Update a customer's loyalty tier based on their points.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE CustomerTiers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    tier_id     INT NOT NULL,
    updated_at  DATETIME NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_tier     FOREIGN KEY (tier_id)     REFERENCES Tiers(tier_id)
);

CREATE VIEW CustomerPointTotals AS
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.email,
       SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
       COUNT(lp.point_id)    AS transaction_count,
       MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
FROM Customers c
JOIN LoyaltyPoints lp ON lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email;

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomerPoints(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT p.customer_id,
           CONCAT(c.first_name, ' ', c.last_name) AS customer_name,
           p.total_points,
           t.tier_name,
           t.benefits
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p
    JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.customer_id = p.customer_id
    JOIN Tiers t ON t.tier_id = ct.tier_id
    WHERE p.customer_id = p_customer_id;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomersInTier(IN p_tier_name VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.first_name,
           c.last_name,
           c.email,
           c.join_date,
           ct.updated_at AS tier_assigned_on
    FROM Tiers t
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
    JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    WHERE t.tier_name = p_tier_name
    ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTotalPointsByCustomer()
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.email,
           SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
           COUNT(lp.point_id) AS transaction_count,
           MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN LoyaltyPoints lp ON lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email
    ORDER BY total_points DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTierSummary()
BEGIN
    SELECT t.tier_name,
           t.min_points,
           COUNT(ct.customer_id) AS member_count,
           ROUND(AVG(p.total_points), 1) AS avg_points
    FROM Tiers t
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
    JOIN CustomerPointTotals p ON p.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    GROUP BY t.tier_id, t.tier_name, t.min_points
    ORDER BY t.min_points;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE UpdateCustomerTier(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO CustomerTiers (customer_id, tier_id, updated_at)
    SELECT p.customer_id, t.tier_id, NOW()
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p
    JOIN Tiers t ON p.total_points BETWEEN t.min_points AND COALESCE(t.max_points, 2147483647)
    WHERE p.customer_id = p_customer_id
    ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE tier_id = VALUES(tier_id), updated_at = NOW();
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE AwardPoints(IN p_customer_id INT, IN p_points INT, IN p_description VARCHAR(255))
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customers WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id) THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Unknown customer_id';
    END IF;
    INSERT INTO LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_earned, transaction_date, description)
    VALUES (p_customer_id, p_points, NOW(), p_description);
    CALL UpdateCustomerTier(p_customer_id);
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL AwardPoints(101, 250, 'Order #5521 - electronics');
CALL AwardPoints(102, 40, 'Order #5522 - groceries');
CALL GetCustomerPoints(101);
CALL GetCustomersInTier('Gold');
CALL GetTotalPointsByCustomer();
CALL GetTierSummary();
text_alt:
CREATE TABLE CustomerTiers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    tier_id     INT NOT NULL,
    updated_at  DATETIME NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_tier     FOREIGN KEY (tier_id)     REFERENCES Tiers(tier_id)
);

CREATE VIEW CustomerPointTotals AS
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.email,
       SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
       COUNT(lp.point_id)    AS transaction_count,
       MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
FROM Customers c, LoyaltyPoints lp
WHERE lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email;

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomerPoints(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT p.customer_id,
           CONCAT(c.first_name, ' ', c.last_name) AS customer_name,
           p.total_points,
           t.tier_name,
           t.benefits
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p, Customers c, CustomerTiers ct, Tiers t
    WHERE c.customer_id = p.customer_id
      AND ct.customer_id = p.customer_id
      AND t.tier_id = ct.tier_id
      AND p.customer_id = p_customer_id;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomersInTier(IN p_tier_name VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.first_name,
           c.last_name,
           c.email,
           c.join_date,
           ct.updated_at AS tier_assigned_on
    FROM Tiers t, CustomerTiers ct, Customers c
    WHERE ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
      AND c.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND t.tier_name = p_tier_name
    ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTotalPointsByCustomer()
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.email,
           SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
           COUNT(lp.point_id) AS transaction_count,
           MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
    FROM Customers c, LoyaltyPoints lp
    WHERE lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email
    ORDER BY total_points DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTierSummary()
BEGIN
    SELECT t.tier_name,
           t.min_points,
           COUNT(ct.customer_id) AS member_count,
           ROUND(AVG(p.total_points), 1) AS avg_points
    FROM Tiers t, CustomerTiers ct, CustomerPointTotals p
    WHERE ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
      AND p.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    GROUP BY t.tier_id, t.tier_name, t.min_points
    ORDER BY t.min_points;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE UpdateCustomerTier(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO CustomerTiers (customer_id, tier_id, updated_at)
    SELECT p.customer_id, t.tier_id, NOW()
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p, Tiers t
    WHERE p.total_points BETWEEN t.min_points AND COALESCE(t.max_points, 2147483647)
      AND p.customer_id = p_customer_id
    ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE tier_id = VALUES(tier_id), updated_at = NOW();
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE AwardPoints(IN p_customer_id INT, IN p_points INT, IN p_description VARCHAR(255))
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customers WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id) THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Unknown customer_id';
    END IF;
    INSERT INTO LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_earned, transaction_date, description)
    VALUES (p_customer_id, p_points, NOW(), p_description);
    CALL UpdateCustomerTier(p_customer_id);
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL AwardPoints(101, 250, 'Order #5521 - electronics');
CALL AwardPoints(102, 40, 'Order #5522 - groceries');
CALL GetCustomerPoints(101);
CALL GetCustomersInTier('Gold');
CALL GetTotalPointsByCustomer();
CALL GetTierSummary();

Schema: 
`Organizations` (organization_id PK, org_name, contact_person, type)
`Grants` (grant_id PK, grant_name, description, available_funds, deadline)
`Applications` (application_id PK, organization_id FK, grant_id FK, submission_date, requested_amount, status)

Queries:
1. List all applications for a specific grant, including organization details.
2. Find all grants with a deadline in the next month.
3. Count the number of applications by status for each grant.
4. Submit a new grant application for an organization.
5. Update the status of an application to 'Approved'.

-- Grant management module: reporting views, lookup procedures and write operations.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_application_detail AS
SELECT a.application_id,
       a.grant_id,
       g.grant_name,
       g.deadline,
       o.organization_id,
       o.org_name,
       o.contact_person,
       o.type AS org_type,
       a.submission_date,
       a.requested_amount,
       a.status
FROM Applications a
JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = a.organization_id;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_application_counts_by_status AS
SELECT g.grant_id, g.grant_name, a.status, COUNT(a.application_id) AS application_count
FROM Grants g
JOIN Applications a ON a.grant_id = g.grant_id
GROUP BY g.grant_id, g.grant_name, a.status;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_grants_due_next_month AS
SELECT g.grant_id, g.grant_name, g.available_funds, g.deadline
FROM Grants g
WHERE g.deadline >= DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE() + INTERVAL 1 MONTH, '%Y-%m-01')
  AND g.deadline <  DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE() + INTERVAL 2 MONTH, '%Y-%m-01');

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE list_applications_for_grant(IN p_grant_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT a.application_id, o.org_name, o.contact_person, o.type AS org_type,
           a.submission_date, a.requested_amount, a.status
    FROM Applications a
    JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = a.organization_id
    WHERE a.grant_id = p_grant_id
    ORDER BY a.submission_date, a.application_id;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE organization_history(IN p_organization_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT a.application_id, g.grant_name, g.deadline,
           a.submission_date, a.requested_amount, a.status
    FROM Applications a
    JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
    WHERE a.organization_id = p_organization_id
    ORDER BY a.submission_date DESC;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE submit_application(IN p_organization_id INT,
                                    IN p_grant_id INT,
                                    IN p_requested_amount DECIMAL(12,2))
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO Applications (organization_id, grant_id, submission_date, requested_amount, status)
    SELECT o.organization_id, g.grant_id, CURDATE(), p_requested_amount, 'Submitted'
    FROM Grants g
    JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = p_organization_id
    WHERE g.grant_id = p_grant_id
      AND g.deadline >= CURDATE()
      AND g.available_funds >= p_requested_amount;

    IF ROW_COUNT() = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Application rejected: unknown organization/grant, past deadline or insufficient funds';
    END IF;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE approve_application(IN p_application_id INT)
BEGIN
    UPDATE Applications a
    JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
    SET a.status = 'Approved',
        g.available_funds = g.available_funds - a.requested_amount
    WHERE a.application_id = p_application_id
      AND a.status <> 'Approved'
      AND g.available_funds >= a.requested_amount;

    IF ROW_COUNT() = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Approval failed: application already approved, missing or funds exhausted';
    END IF;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL submit_application(3, 7, 25000.00);
CALL approve_application(LAST_INSERT_ID());
CALL list_applications_for_grant(7);
CALL organization_history(3);
SELECT * FROM v_grants_due_next_month;
SELECT * FROM v_application_counts_by_status WHERE grant_id = 7;
SELECT * FROM v_application_detail WHERE organization_id = 3;

Schema: 
`Games` (game_id PK, game_name, genre, release_year)
`Players` (player_id PK, username, join_date)
`HighScores` (score_id PK, game_id FK, player_id FK, score, achieve_date)

Queries:
1. Get the top 10 high scores for a specific game, including player usernames.
2. Find all high scores achieved by a specific player.
3. Count the number of scores submitted for each game.
4. Record a new high score for a player in a game.
5. Update a player's high score for a specific game if the new score is higher.
text_nat:
-- Arcade high-score module: leaderboard views and the five required operations.

-- Leaderboard view: every score with its game and player details, ranked per game.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_game_leaderboard AS
SELECT g.game_id,
       g.game_name,
       g.genre,
       p.player_id,
       p.username,
       h.score,
       h.achieve_date,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g.game_id
                    ORDER BY h.score DESC, h.achieve_date ASC) AS rank_in_game
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id;

-- Per-game score volume; subqueries keep games that have never been played.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_game_score_counts AS
SELECT g.game_id,
       g.game_name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HighScores h WHERE h.game_id = g.game_id) AS score_count,
       (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(h.score), 0) FROM HighScores h WHERE h.game_id = g.game_id) AS best_score
FROM Games g;

-- 1. Top 10 high scores for a specific game, with player usernames.
SELECT p.username, h.score, h.achieve_date
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id
WHERE g.game_id = 3
ORDER BY h.score DESC, h.achieve_date ASC
LIMIT 10;

-- 2. All high scores achieved by a specific player.
SELECT p.username, g.game_name, g.genre, g.release_year, h.score, h.achieve_date
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id
WHERE h.player_id = 17
ORDER BY h.achieve_date DESC, h.score DESC;

-- 3. Number of scores submitted for each game.
SELECT game_id, game_name, score_count, best_score
FROM v_game_score_counts
ORDER BY score_count DESC, game_name;

-- 4. Record a new high score; the join rejects unknown ids and pre-join dates.
INSERT INTO HighScores (game_id, player_id, score, achieve_date)
SELECT g.game_id, p.player_id, 48200, DATE '2024-05-02'
FROM Games g
JOIN Players p ON p.join_date <= DATE '2024-05-02'
WHERE g.game_id = 3 AND p.player_id = 17;

-- 5. Raise a player's score for a game (identified by name) only if the run is better.
UPDATE HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
SET h.score = 51750,
    h.achieve_date = DATE '2024-06-11'
WHERE h.player_id = 17
  AND g.game_name = 'Nebula Rally'
  AND h.score < 51750;

-- Report: current leader of every game next to that game's score volume.
SELECT c.game_name, c.score_count, l.username AS leader, l.score AS leading_score
FROM v_game_score_counts c
JOIN v_game_leaderboard l ON l.game_id = c.game_id AND l.rank_in_game = 1
ORDER BY l.score DESC;

-- Report: genre totals built from the ranked leaderboard rows.
SELECT l.genre,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.game_id) AS games_played,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.player_id) AS players,
       MAX(l.score) AS genre_record
FROM v_game_leaderboard l
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = l.player_id
WHERE p.join_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY l.genre
ORDER BY genre_record DESC;
